articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: This is the Meta MetaRoCE Network Adapter
articles.summary:
At OCP Summit 2026, we saw Meta’s new MetaRoCE network adapter. This is Meta’s answer to providing an open RDMA transport layer that has features like packet spraying, congestion control, and more. This was a presentation we saw at OCP Summit, but Meta had a NIC on display.
Meta MetaRoCE Network Adapter at OCP 2026
Here is the display from the Meta booth at OCP Summit 2026, where you can see an OCP NIC 3.0 card.
During its OCP 2026 presentation, Meta shared some of the big features of MetaRoCE:
- Per-path reliability and congestion control
- Receiver rate hints (RCN) for fast incast convergence
- Tolerates packet loss and reordering
- Single QP carries multiple streams over multiple network paths
- Runs on commodity Ethernet: ECN + ECMP, no switch (Source: Meta)
Before OCP Summit, Meta demonstrated this with the AMD Pensando NIC series. The programmability allowed it to implement the protocol without having dedicated hardware. That allows Meta to potentially source from multiple vendors.
Meta is trying to build a network protocol that can scale to million-GPU training, but also that can run on different network topologies and hardware.
As a quick aside, the NIC shown was an OCP NIC 3.0 with SFF pull tab design, which is our favorite form factor that we wish all server vendors used.

articles.title: Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills
articles.summary:
Build once, run on any agent: A practical guide to agent skills
Agent skills capture repeatable engineering work in files teams can review and reuse, while tools, project context, and permissions remain specific to the host that runs them.
How many times this week did you re-explain the same task to an agent? How many times did you ask your colleague with deep institutional knowledge how to solve a specific problem? That context shouldn’t be lost in a chat or locked in one person’s head. Agent skills let you capture repeatable instructions so you and your agents can reuse them. The skill you write for yourself tonight can later become part of a team’s pipeline.
An agent skill is a versioned directory centered on a SKILL.md file that describes when and how to do a repeatable task. You can share those instructions across agents, but the environment still needs to provide the tools, credentials, and permissions to carry them out. A skill can describe how to query a database, for example, but it doesn’t grant access to that database.
A skill works best when it has a clear job, input, and output. For example, let’s say you’re building an agent that checks AI-generated changes against the original request. If the same agent assesses its own work, its explanation might influence the review. With Proof Agent, we use a separate verifier to examine the changes and provide evidence for its findings. The skill’s frontmatter names the task and describes its purpose:

articles.title: The promise and peril of AI in government
articles.summary:
In Taoyuan, Taiwan’s bustling industrial hub where 200 semiconductor manufacturing facilities are based, Mayor San-Cheng Chang is using AI to orchestrate an ambitious transformation. He brings a unique blend of technical expertise and government experience to the challenge of running the country’s fastest-growing city. Before becoming mayor, he served as Taiwan’s first nonpartisan premier and held leadership positions at both Google and Acer. As a former director of Taiwan’s National Center for High-Performance Computing, Chang embodies the intersection of technology and governance that helps explain Taoyuan’s embrace of AI.
As the home of Taiwan’s international airport as well as 2.2 million residents, Taoyuan must manage heavy truck traffic, air pollution, rapid population growth, and constant construction. Since March 2023, Taoyuan has run an AI-powered lung cancer screening initiative targeting citizens over 40 with risk factors that include occupational exposure and family history. Two years later, Taoyuan’s program had screened over 400,000 residents, detecting 233 lung cancer cases (90% in early stage), and achieving cost savings of NT$500 million ($17 million) through AI-aided diagnostics. articles.title: Un ‘USB’ universal de creación europea para dar una segunda vida a los satélites y reducir la basura espacial
articles.summary:
Un ‘USB’ universal de creación europea para dar una segunda vida a los satélites y reducir la basura espacial
Un grupo de investigadores desarrolla y prueba un sistema similar a estos puertos de conexión que podría facilitar la reparación de estos artefactos en órbita
¿No resulta molesto tener que viajar con varios adaptadores durante las vacaciones? Pues lo mismo ocurre en el espacio, donde las naves espaciales y los satélites suelen utilizar diferentes conectores para transmitir energía, datos y otros servicios. Un equipo internacional de investigadores ha estado estudiando si una interfaz común puede facilitar estas conexiones. Su idea, desarrollada en el marco del proyecto Space USB, financiado por la UE, se parece un poco a los puertos USB tan extendidos en el ámbito informático: una conexión normalizada admite diferentes funciones en diversos diseños de satélites.
“Es algo que nos concierne a todos”, afirma Raphael Boissonnade, de Thales Alenia Space en Francia, quien coordinó el proyecto. “Ofrecemos los mismos enchufes, pero con servicios y tecnología diferentes”. Esta flexibilidad es cada vez más necesaria. En la actualidad, hay más de 16.000 satélites orbitando la Tierra, y su número sigue aumentando. Sin embargo, cuando un satélite se queda sin combustible o su equipamiento queda obsoleto, lo habitual es sustituirlo en lugar de repararlo o actualizarlo en órbita.
Esto genera costes y riesgos. Un satélite que ya no puede maniobrar puede convertirse en basura espacial…

articles.title: Cyberattack on Fireworks AI allowed hackers to access Notion customers' chat transcripts | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
A cyberattack at Fireworks AI has exposed some of its customers’ data, the company has confirmed. Fireworks AI, a platform that developers use to access and use open AI models, said an attacker breached its cloud provider to gain access to a Fireworks development system, which allowed access to some of its customers’ data.
The company said in its latest security advisory that the cybercriminals took Fireworks’ customers’ billing information and some datasets. Fireworks touts tens of thousands of customers worldwide using its platform, including legal tech company Harvey and AI company Cursor.
At least one confirmed affected customer is online document editor and notetaker Notion, which said in a disclosure that the breach affected around 1% of its own customers.
Notion said that Fireworks alerted the company to a security incident and later confirmed that the hackers had stolen some Notion customer data. On November 3, Notion said it disconnected its systems from Fireworks, deleted the data stored in its systems, and stopped all connectivity between the two.
Notion confirmed this week that the hackers took chat transcripts of its Notion AI customers who used the “Insights” feature. The company said that the transcripts include “any input to or output from the model that was written to the chat,” but added that much of the data was unattributable and could not be determined from which customer it was obtained.

Im Podcast t3n MeisterPrompter erklärt sie mit t3n-Redakteurin Stella-Sophie Wojtczak, wie sich beide unterscheiden.
/plan und /goal nutzen
Im Planmodus werden dir bei ChatGPT laut Renate gezielt Rückfragen gestellt. Darauf basierend entsteht dann ein Plan. Im Vergleich mit einem einfachen Prompt seien die Fragen im Planmodus laut Renate direkt fokussierter.
Aktivierst du den Zielmodus, beschreibst du ChatGPT oder Claude lediglich dein Ziel, inklusiv der beschreibenden Kriterien. Die KI arbeitet dann auf dieses Ergebniss hin, auch über mehrere Schritte. In ChatGPT waren die Modi wie /study zum lernen bisher auch über die Vorauswahl erreichbar, das gelingt allerdings aktuell nicht.
Am einfachsten ist es dabei, diese Chatvorgabe mit /plan und /goal anzufordern. Das funktioniert laut Renate Tool-übergreifend. Selbstläufer sind die Modi jedoch nicht. articles.title: Hackers Deploy Malware in Fresh ScreenConnect Campaign
articles.summary:
A threat actor has compromised hundreds of endpoints across dozens of ConnectWise ScreenConnect customers in a fresh campaign, cybersecurity outfit Huntress reports.
The attacks were observed on November 11, when the hackers abused their unauthorized access to cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to run commands on managed endpoints.
According to Huntress, the campaign compromised at least 6 MSPs and 288 hosts across 48 organizations. The attackers hit all 288 compromised hosts within 90 minutes.
The attackers’ commands deployed rogue ScreenConnect clients and a malware toolkit called SCKit that provides persistent backdoor access, intercepts session cookies, and can self-replicate.
Initially deployed via ScreenConnect panels, it waits for a technician to connect to the compromised endpoint to infect their workstation. Next, attempts to compromise other sessions the technician has access to and spread itself to other panels.
“However, not all functionality has been observed during observed incidents; some functionality has been discovered through analyzing the payloads,” Huntress says.
As part of the attacks, the hackers exploited a vulnerability in RMM+, a third-party extension for managing ScreenConnect sessions that uses a shared access key to bypass ScreenConnect’s authentication mechanism.
The hackers likely exploited a bug in the extension’s versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32, where the access key defaults to blank if not configured, thus allowing an attacker to bypass authenticat…

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert…

Le retour aux sources, motivé par une envie de nostalgie, fonctionne, et Blizzard revendique déjà le plus gros lancement de l’histoire de World of Warcraft, avec un pic de joueurs connectés jamais vu pour un lancement du jeu (sans toutefois publier le moindre chiffre). Contrairement àWorld of Warcraft et World of Warcraft: Classic, World of Warcraft: Forever ne convertit pas les points d’expérience en pièces d’or une fois le niveau maximum atteint. Cette fonctionnalité avait été introduite en 2006, quelques semaines avant la sortie de Burning Crusade (janvier 2007), pour permettre aux joueuses et aux joueurs de remplir leur compte en banque en prévision de la sortie de la première extension.
Cette absence est assumée par Blizzard, qui a quand même déployé un correctif ce mercredi 11 novembre pour répondre aux plaintes.

El cerebro tiene que hacer cierto esfuerzo para transformar unos trazos en letras, estas en palabras, darles un significado y combinarlas hasta crear una trama compleja y emocional. articles.summary:
GitHub availability report: October 2026
In October, we experienced eight incidents that resulted in degraded performance across GitHub services.
We continue to share monthly updates on the work behind GitHub’s availability and reliability.
The short version of October: we added substantial independently scalable Azure capacity and removed several ways that failures could escalate. However, write outages, monitoring gaps during data migrations, and a regional network disruption reinforced the need for capacity growth to be paired with safer operations, stronger isolation, and validated regional recovery.
As of November 9, 140 of 151 production services and 32 of 50 MySQL primaries were running in Azure Central US. Azure served 63% of migrated-service reads, 66% of monolith reads, and 52% of Git reads. We also completed a compute expansion across all nine Central US Kubernetes clusters, more than doubling capacity.
That capacity is already carrying real growth. Migrated-service traffic has increased 82% since March, with Central US absorbing the growth beyond the highest weekly-average load previously served from our existing datacenter. This gives GitHub more room to grow without pushing the original environment beyond its prior operating range.

articles.title: Notion Customer Data Compromised in Fireworks AI Hack
articles.summary:
All-in-one collaborative workspace and productivity platform Notion is notifying a small set of customers that their information was compromised in a data breach involving Fireworks AI.
A cloud platform for running and fine-tuning open source AI models, Fireworks AI was hacked twice in October: once through compromised internal credentials, and once through a third-party cloud provider that was hosting Fireworks R&D machines.
The second incident, linked to a recent rise in LLMJacking activity, occurred on October 24, when the attackers executed an unauthorized workload leading to the compromise of customer data.
Fireworks contained the incident the same day and notified Notion on November 2 that Notion AI data had been accessed. Prior to the incident, Notion used Fireworks as a general inference provider for delivering open-weight models.
Notion’s investigation into the compromised data determined that the hackers accessed Notion AI chat transcripts used for the Insights feature, which helps customers understand their AI usage.
Fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces were affected, and most of the transcripts were unattributable to a customer or the workspace they came from.
“Beyond what’s in the chat transcript itself, there’s no information tying the chat back to workspaces, users or companies,” Notion says.

Le cofondateur a donc été poussé vers la sortie après des révélations sur deux liaisons présumées, dont l’une avec une femme soupçonnée d’espionnage pour le compte de la Chine.
Pour le remplacer, le conseil a choisi Colette Kress, la femme qui tient les finances de Nvidia depuis treize ans. Sa mission est toutefois temporaire : selon le communiqué, le conseil a lancé le recrutement d’un PDG permanent et étudiera des candidatures internes comme externes.
Une première en 33 ans

Dans le même communiqué, le conseil a aussi nommé Harvey C. Jones à un poste qui n’existait pas jusqu’ici : président du conseil d’administration. Selon Harvey Jones, cité dans le communiqué, Colette Kress a contribué à mener Nvidia « à travers une période de croissance extraordinaire ».

A quantum computer might seem to have little in common with a guitar, but researchers at ETH Zurich have found a surprising connection. Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.
By harnessing these vibrations, the researchers have created a way for quantum computers to process information efficiently while accessing a flexible working memory. articles.title: Foundation IP For The AI Era: Why Execution Shapes SoC Cost ─ eBook
articles.summary:
How an integrated foundation IP strategy can reduce execution risk, enable faster tape-out, and lower TCO.
As AI workloads push power, performance, voltage, and process variation to new limits, the economics of advanced-node SoCs are changing. In addition to the cost of the IP itself, hidden costs often arrive later in the design cycle: integration delays, schedule slips, re-spins, and missed market windows. As design complexity rises, predictable execution is becoming a critical factor in total cost of ownership (TCO) alongside power, performance, and area (PPA).
Sourcing Foundation IP piece by piece can add another layer of complexity. Logic libraries, embedded memories, I/Os, and OTP NVM IP from multiple suppliers bring different deliverables, roadmaps, support models, and integration requirements. An integrated Foundation IP platform can reduce these seams by bringing the core building blocks together as one silicon-proven, verified stack, with sign-off-ready characterization and IP + EDA co-optimization to improve PPA and accelerate implementation. This tighter alignment helps design teams move toward tape-out with greater predictability.
The impact extends beyond integration. Across HPC and Edge AI designs, improvements in PPA can translate into meaningful economic value through smaller die area, lower operating power, and increased performance, while avoiding a re-spin or major tape-out delay can protect even more value. The Nvidia Board of Directors announced on Thursday morning that the company’s co-founder and CEO of 33 years, Jensen Huang, has resigned as president, CEO, and member of the board, effective immediately.

Few people would have predicted this turn of events even just a week ago, as Huang has been so central to Nvidia throughout the company’s existence that he never even established a succession plan. While the company conducts a more thorough search for Huang’s successor, Nvidia CFO and Executive Vice President Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO. But beyond her name and job title, what do we know about the person who will now lead a company worth about $3.8 trillion?

Before that, she spent three years as an SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology Operations Finance organization. She also worked at Microsoft for 13 years, where she spent four years as CFO of the Server and Tools division. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.

Secure, governed AI protects evidential integrity in sensitive investigations
An investigation into the alleged misuse of AI at Derbyshire Constabulary, arriving alongside wider scrutiny of generative tools across UK policing, has raised an uncomfortable question that extends far beyond the force.
What happens when powerful technology enters any organization where sensitive information is used to support decisions that may later need to be explained and defended?
The answer is not to keep AI out of investigations, intelligence or other high-stakes work, but to deploy it in ways that can withstand scrutiny. Within secure, auditable systems, with clear boundaries and human oversight, AI tools can help organizations connect information, manage growing caseloads and identify important patterns while ensuring that every insight can be traced, explained and defended.
The risk arises when employees turn to general-purpose tools that were never designed to meet those evidential and security standards.

Before companies can deploy smart machines, such as robots or self-driving cars, into the real world, they must understand how these systems will operate under both normal and abnormal conditions. articles.title: Hackers plant GSocket on Linux servers for persistent access
articles.summary:
Multiple threat actors are abusing GSocket, a legitimate open-source remote access tool, to maintain access to Linux servers even after patching the vulnerabilities exploited to gain initial access.
Since March, detections of malicious GSocket activity have increased, particularly in attacks targeting web applications and hosting environments.
GSocket allows attackers to reach systems behind firewalls or NAT by intercepting network connections and replacing the program's conventional IP-layer communication with its own transport layer, which routes traffic through the Global Socket Relay Network.
Since both endpoints initiate outbound connections to the relay, which matches them and brokers an end-to-end encrypted session, an attacker can reconnect without needing the compromised server's IP address or hostname.
This makes it more difficult for defenders to disrupt attacks using IP- or domain-based access control lists.
According to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint telemetry, GSocket-related detections increased by 356.2% between March and August.
Microsoft explains that both the compromised server and the attacker connect outbound, hence the server needs no inbound listener implants, making the attack stealthier.
“The compromised host and the operator both connect outbound to the relay, which bridges the two sessions,” Microsoft explains.
“The host needs no inbound listener or public IP address, and network address translation does not prevent the connection.”

The requests were used to establish whether the stolen access permitted changes to a repository. “The pull request does nothing by itself,” StepSecurity explained, noting that malware was subsequently deployed in repositories where the permissions and configuration allowed it.
Aikido found signs that the stealer ran in more than 1,800 repositories. SafeDep separately counted 8,093 public repositories that received malicious commits, a figure that does not necessarily indicate successful execution.

articles.title: LinkedIn Replaces Argo CD with a Custom GitOps Engine for Kubernetes Deployments
articles.summary:
In a recent post, LinkedIn revealed it has replaced Argo CD with its own GitOps engine. This new system deploys applications across over 250 Kubernetes clusters. It supports more than 4,000 services and manages over 100,000 deployments each week. According to a post, deployment infrastructure failures fell from 925 to 63 despite a 3.7x increase in deployment volume. The median time to detect and conclude a failed deployment dropped from 16.1 to 2.45 minutes.
LinkedIn started with one Argo CD instance per cluster, a topology it chose because Argo CD already managed its cluster add-ons that way. Clusters run up to 5,000 nodes each. A central deployment orchestrator spawned an ephemeral pod per deployment, with Argo CD hidden behind it. The team lists seven problems that emerged at scale. Argo CD doesn't have an observedGeneration, so you can't link sync and health status to a specific deployment. LinkedIn created a Lua health check that uses a tracking annotation to address this. A Synced and Healthy application could also resolve to an unintended revision when stale repo-server cache entries were used.
Two of the issues were architectural. Argo CD maintains one watch per group-version-resource across Applications. LinkedIn’s clusters have low resource-type diversity. This means etcd churn from one app can slow syncs for all apps. In one test, sync took under 3 minutes on a cluster with 60,000 pods and over 10 minutes with more than 80,000. Se trata del hecho de que la pensión calculada tenga que ser superior a la mínima a la que tendría derecho el solicitante a los 65 años de edad (teniendo en cuenta su situación familiar).
En esta modalidad se puede adelantar el retiro máximo hasta dos años antes de la edad ordinaria correspondiente. Además, hacen falta al menos 35 años de cotización efectiva. Ejemplo de cuantía para 2026
Por ejemplo, un trabajador de 63 años tiene 40 cotizados y tiene una pensión calculada de 1.058 € mensuales. Vive con su mujer, que no trabaja y no tiene pensión.

articles.title: Introduction To FP8 Formats: Part 1
articles.summary:
The rationale behind 8-bit floating-point data formats, their ecosystem momentum, and hardware support.
The industry is moving from high-precision formats (FP32, FP16, BF16) to lower-precision data types for Machine Learning (ML) inference and training. In cloud and data center environments, lower-precision data types deliver higher throughput by packing more compute per cycle from the same platform. On edge and mobile devices, smaller formats reduce model size, memory footprint and bandwidth, which directly affects power consumption and latency.
Arm, Intel, and NVIDIA published an OCP 8-bit Floating Point Specification (OFP8). It is an interchange format that allows software systems to share the models easily. FP8 is not a future concept, it is being deployed today. It is already supported by NVIDIA’s Hopper H100 GPU, with software deployment appearing in major ML frameworks.
Arm added the FP8 support to the Arm v9 ISA and is exploring the best way to integrate the FP8 across all the ML platforms.
This blog post explains the FP8 data formats, the new Floating-point Mode Register (FPMR), and the instruction set that makes FP8 practical on Arm CPUs.
Unlike IEEE FP64, FP32, and FP16, FP8 is not a single format, it is a family. The whitepaper FP8 Formats for Deep Learning proposes an FP8 format consisting of two encodings: E4M3 and E5M2.
With only 8 bits available, FP8 makes a trade-off between precision and dynamic range. A single encoding cannot fit all tensors equally well. A…

articles.title: Trump floats Apple chairman Tim Cook as Jensen Huang's successor | TechCrunch

In the wake of the industry-shaking news of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation on Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump is floating the idea that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over the position.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that “only one man” could take Huang’s place: Tim Cook of Apple.
“A Legend replaces a Legend!” he wrote.
Cook stepped down as Apple’s CEO on September 1, 2026, after 15 years running the company, but he’s still very much involved with Apple. While John Ternus took over as Apple’s CEO, Cook transitioned into the role of executive chairman of Apple’s board of directors, which sees him continuing to engage with global policymakers and manage international relationships, including Apple’s relations with China.
Trump is not the only one to suggest Cook as a replacement for Huang. Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, Senior Associate Dean for Leadership Studies at Yale School of Management, who studies CEO leadership and corporate governance, penned an op-ed in Time on Wednesday, suggesting Cook should be among the potential candidates. articles.title: El país sin mar que más se acerca a tener una costa: hizo el negocio del siglo al ceder un tramo de carretera a Ucrania antes de que llegara Rusia
articles.summary:
Cuando la Unión Soviética se desintegró en 1991, Moldavia se convirtió en un país independiente con un pequeño problema geográfico: tenía el mar Negro prácticamente a las puertas, pero carecía de litoral. Ocho años después, sus dirigentes encontraron una solución que pasaba por un insólito intercambio territorial con Ucrania. Moldavia cedió un trozo de carretera y recibió a cambio unos cientos de metros de ribera. Aquella operación terminaría convirtiéndose en uno de los negocios más importantes de su historia.
A las puertas del mar. Encajada entre Rumanía y Ucrania, Moldavia ocupa una superficie de 33.846 kilómetros cuadrados y carece de costa marítima. Su extremo meridional, sin embargo, alcanza uno de los grandes corredores comerciales de Europa: el Danubio, el segundo río más largo del continente, que desemboca en el mar Negro.
Durante sus primeros años de independencia, Moldavia dependía de sus vecinos para buena parte de sus importaciones y exportaciones. articles.title: The Memory Challenge Of Physical AI
articles.summary:
Right-size the memory hierarchy around the device’s data streams, reuse patterns, latency requirements, and operating constraints.
Most AI hardware conversations start with compute, which is understandable since accelerators are visible, easy to compare, and often tied to headline performance metrics. Physical AI broadens that conversation by placing greater emphasis on how compute, memory, and data movement work together under real-world operating constraints. For intelligent systems that must see, interpret, decide, and act in the physical world in real time, it’s critical that the right data reaches the right engine at the right time.
As a result, data movement has become an increasingly important consideration when architecting physical AI systems. A physical AI device may simultaneously handle sensor streams, model weights, activations, temporary buffers, control loops, and safety functions. If memory access becomes unpredictable, compute engines can stall. Power consumption rises when data is moved too often, and poorly planned buffering can cause latency accumulation that is hard to recover from later.
As physical AI workloads become more complex, architects must now consider how predictably the complete system performs when multiple real-world workloads are active simultaneously.
Physical AI systems rely on a memory hierarchy that coordinates on-chip memory with larger-capacity external memory. LPDDR or GDDR may hold model weights, sensor data, activations, and other …

Instructors provide the platform with course materials, assignments, and grading criteria, which the software uses to question students about their work. At Sprint Technology Solutions we had several products, and each one ended up with its own copy of the same financial validation, sort code checks in one place, IBAN formatting in another, card validation somewhere else, all written slightly differently by whoever got there first.
The moment it really landed for me was on a payout flow. We had account and sort code validation on the web side, and then the mobile app needed the same thing. Rather than share it, the validation got rewritten for mobile, and the two copies drifted. One of them was a little stricter than the other, so a bank detail that the web form accepted would get rejected on mobile, and we had people re-entering details that were actually fine. It took longer than it should have to track down, because nobody thinks to check whether two "identical" validators are actually identical. The fix was easy once we found it, but the real problem was that there were two of them at all.

Mafia: The Old Country emmène la saga là où tout a commencé, dans la Sicile du début des années 1900, plusieurs décennies avant le premier épisode. articles.title: Entró en vigor: los propietarios no están obligados a pagar las cuotas de la comunidad pendientes si han pasado 5 años
articles.summary:
Si tienes cuotas de la comunidad pendientes desde hace años, debes saber que eso no significa que tengas que pagarlas. Así, si la comunidad no ha realizado reclamaciones dentro del plazo legal, puede perder el derecho a exigirlas, pero para ello hay que comprobar dos cosas: cuándo vencieron los recibos y si existió algún tipo de reclamación.
Como recoge El Español en su información sobre las cuotas comunitarias, el Tribunal Supremo confirmó en varias sentencias que el plazo pasa de 15 años a solo 5. De esta forma, el tiempo anterior baja una década y la clave está en que esas cuotas ahora tienen su propia regulación al considerarse pagos periódicos.
Así, el artículo 1966.3 del Código Civil establece 5 años para reclamar cantidades que se deban abonar anualmente o en periodos más cortos. El Supremo reiteró esta interpretación en varias resoluciones, pero hay un detalle importante: el plazo se puede interrumpir si la comunidad reclama la deuda judicial o extrajudicialmente, o si el propio propietario la reconoce. Por eso, no basta con que un recibo tenga más de 5 años para considerarlo prescrito.
A todo esto debemos sumar que la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal obliga a los propietarios a contribuir a los gastos generales del edificio entre los que se incluyen, por ejemplo, servicios y cargas comunes. articles.title: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates cause SQL Server performance issues
articles.summary:
Microsoft has confirmed that Windows updates released since the October 2026 Patch Tuesday are causing SQL Server performance and stability issues.
As detailed in a Windows release health dashboard update on Wednesday, this is caused by server queries that leave connections open after the queries complete. These connections accumulate instead of closing, degrading server performance over time.
"This issue affects SQL Server linked server queries that use OLE DB providers to connect to external databases. Oracle and PostgreSQL connections are among those known to be affected," Microsoft explained.
"In affected environments, administrators might observe an increasing number of open connections to external databases, even when the associated SQL Server linked server queries are no longer running."
It also added that admins may be able to manually close connections left open due to this bug or restart the SQL service to temporarily address stability and performance issues, but this can also kill active queries and may not fully address the issue, as it will resurface again after some time.
Microsoft says the issues impact both client (Windows 10 and Windows 11) and server (Windows Server 2012 and later) systems and will be fixed with an out-of-band Windows update to be released over the next few days.
While it works to resolve the bug, Microsoft said IT administrators can reach out to Microsoft Support for Business for a mitigation that can address the issue until a fix is availa…

articles.title: IP Integration Challenges Evolve
articles.summary:
Integration challenges are growing more complex, but the problem is well understood and solutions are emerging.
Key Takeaways:
IP integration is not the most glamorous task in semiconductor design, but it often is one of the most troublesome. At the intersection of block-level verification and system-level interactions, bugs are often very difficult to find.
The creation of the Virtual Socket Interface Alliance (VSIA) in 1996 was, for many, the first time the notion of designing a system by integrating third-party IP blocks became a reality. Its charter was to unify and standardize the way IP was constructed, verified, delivered, and supported. The alliance dissolved in 2008, considering its work to either be complete, or transferring parts of it to other organizations that were more focused on specific pieces of the problem. Eighteen years later, the problem continues to evolve.
The idea was that each company should focus on developing the part of the design that was novel and unique, adding their expertise, and allowing the rest to be developed by domain experts.
“Ten years ago, a design may have had tens of IP blocks,” says Pedro Pires, SOS product manager at Keysight EDA. “Today, a company may have thousands of IPs, dozens of different versions of the same IP, and you want to make sense of all of this. articles.title: Google Open-Sources TPU Sync for KV Cache and Weight Transfer on TPUs
articles.summary:
Google Cloud has open-sourced TPU Sync, a native C++ library that moves KV cache blocks and model weights between TPU HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and the data center network. GCP also announced the TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max systems, the project targets two workloads where accelerators often wait on data: long-context and disaggregated LLM serving, and reinforcement learning loops that push updated weights from trainers to rollout samplers.
For prefill/decode disaggregation, Google says median KV transfer latency for Qwen3 235B fell from several seconds to about 230 ms, with average TTFT reductions of 60% for that model and 90% for a 480B model at low concurrency. For prefix caching, it reports up to 90% lower average TTFT on 64K-context workloads.
Developers get Python wheels for JAX and PyTorch, with KV cache manager, KV store, and weight synchronizer APIs. TPU Sync acts as the KV connector for vLLM-TorchTPU through vLLM's KVConnector interface, as the disaggregation and hierarchical-cache backend for SGLang-TorchTPU, and pairs with llm-d 1.0 on GKE for prefix-cache-aware routing. The RL weight-sync module for Pathways and multi-controller JAX is experimental. The GitHub repository, which absorbed the earlier TPU Raiden codebase, warns that APIs are changing rapidly and that only development builds are on PyPI, and recommends pinning to its last-known-good commit. articles.title: Un comando de Windows para liberar 10 GB de espacio en el disco duro
articles.summary:
Cuando el disco duro principal empieza a quedarse sin espacio, solemos buscar qué carpetas del sistema están devorando nuestros gigas. Y es que, si revisamos a fondo la partición del sistema, no es raro encontrarse con que la carpeta WinSxS ha ido creciendo con el paso de las semanas hasta ocupar 10 GB, 12 GB o incluso más de 20 GB sin que nos hayamos dado cuenta.
El almacén del sistema. WinSxS funciona como un repositorio interno de componentes de Microsoft. Su función principal es la de conservar versiones paralelas de diferentes archivos esenciales y librerías DLL para evitar conflictos de compatibilidad, y permitir recuperar versiones anteriores tras cada actualización. El sistema una tarea automática para hacer limpieza llamada StartComponentCleanup, pero no se activa hasta que pasan 30 días enteros tras una actualización, pero si necesitas espacio urgentemente puedes lanzarlo manualmente.
Comprobar el peso real. Muchos de los archivos que residen dentro de WinSxS están vinculados con la carpeta System32, lo que provoca que las propiedades convencionales de Windows Explorer muestren un cálculo distorsionado del espacio. Para salir de dudas y comprobar exactamente cuánto almacenamiento puedes recuperar, basta con abrir PowerShell o el Símbolo del sistema con permisos de administrador y ejecutar el siguiente comando:
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /AnalyzeComponentStore
Windows se pondrá a analizar el almacén de componentes, y te dirá el tamaño real que ocupa en el disco, dic…

La clave está en asegurar una conexión estable y evitar condiciones que eleven la temperatura del teléfono. La guía de YUP Charge reúne diferentes prácticas que ayudan a aprovechar mejor cada carga y a preservar el funcionamiento de la batería con el paso del tiempo.
Por qué se debe elegir un cargador original
El cargador y el cable determinan la potencia que recibe el celular. Usar accesorios certificados por el fabricante o por marcas reconocidas permite que el dispositivo regule la energía según sus especificaciones.
Muchos cargadores rápidos ofrecen entre 18W y 65W, aunque la velocidad final depende de lo que admita cada modelo de teléfono. La potencia más alta no siempre significa una carga más rápida si el dispositivo no es compatible con ese estándar.
Un adaptador de baja calidad, deteriorado o incompatible puede prolongar la carga, provocar interrupciones y elevar la temperatura. Conviene revisar el estado del cable: si presenta dobleces pronunciadas, conectores flojos o daños visibles, puede afectar la transmisión de energía.

articles.title: Apache Patches Critical HTTP Server RCE Found by Anthropic, Google
articles.summary:
Apache has patched a critical HTTP Server vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE), following independent discoveries by Anthropic and Google researchers.
Tracked as CVE-2026-119618, the flaw affects Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70. The issue was addressed on November 11 with the release of version 2.4.71. It resides in mod_http2, the module responsible for handling HTTP/2 traffic.
The vulnerability involves a race condition in which multiple threads improperly access shared resources, potentially corrupting server memory.
According to Red Hat, an attacker could exploit the issue remotely without authentication to execute arbitrary commands and gain control of the server process. Red Hat assigned the vulnerability a CVSS score of 9.8 and explained that “only servers that have HTTP/2 enabled are affected; servers configured to serve only HTTP/1.1 are not vulnerable.”
Apache credited Anthropic’s OSS Scanner with reporting the flaw on October 26. Anthony Weems and Simon Scannell of Google Cloud Vulnerability Research independently reported the same vulnerability on November 3.
Cloud security firm Wiz reported that 64% of cloud environments in its data contained resources running affected Apache versions, while 51% had publicly exposed instances. The company cautioned that these figures do not account for server configuration, so they do not necessarily represent exploitable installations.

Le coupable, AMD External Events Utility, sert notamment à faire fonctionner FreeSync, la technologie qui cale le rafraîchissement de l’écran sur les images envoyées par la carte.

Ses notes de version citent deux problèmes réglés : des « écritures excessives sur le disque système » au repos, sur les Radeon RX 7000 et plus récentes, et des écritures du même genre au moindre déplacement d’une fenêtre.

articles.title: Hundreds of streaming services and nothing to watch
articles.summary:
“Fifty-seven channels, and nothin’ on.”
Bruce Springsteen famously said those words during a concert and later in a song in the 1990s about the number of TV channels seemingly growing disproportionately to the availability of enjoyable content.
Within a few years, there would be hundreds of TV channels and still, some would argue in hyperbolic frustration, “nothing to watch.”
The advent of streaming services was poised as a potential solution to this problem. It granted viewers easy, on-demand access to thousands of movies and shows, which, theoretically, could ensure that viewers could always find something to watch.
According to a survey from Nielsen’s Gracenote, though, that’s not exactly the case today.
Gracenote, a Nielsen-owned content data business, surveyed 3,000 video streaming users in the US, Brazil, France, Germany, Mexico, and the UK who were at least 18 years old for its “2026 State of Play: Amid fragmentation frustrations, UX is the future of streaming” report. It found that many struggle to find something to stream. However, this is not necessarily because there’s nothing good on, but rather because they find it difficult to home in on good content on streaming services.
For example, over 51 percent of respondents said that “the abundance of content and [streaming] services is making it harder to find something to watch.”

articles.title: Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before Congress, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said on Thursday, according to reports from Bloomberg and NBC News.
Huang, who stepped down as CEO following reports of an alleged affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, agreed to testify Wednesday after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.
Huang has agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, which falls later this month.
The development comes after House Republicans Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford sent Huang a letter on November 4 requesting that he appear before their committees. Moolenaar chairs the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, Mast chairs the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and Crawford chairs the House Intelligence Committee.
“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”
The testimony will take place behind closed doors, though Mast said he expects the briefing to be recorded on video and transcribed.

articles.title: Nigerians can pay without cards or transfers, yet remain completely unaware
articles.summary:
The next time a point-of-sale (PoS) agent asks for a bank card, inserting it may not be necessary. Some Nigerian cards can already complete transactions with a single tap.
TechCabal tested this at a local PoS merchant. Using a Verve debit card issued through ALAT, the digital banking platform of tier-2 Nigerian lender Wema Bank, the team held the card near the terminal instead of inserting it. The machine recognised the card, requested a PIN, and dispensed ₦1,500 ($1.11) from the ₦1,600 ($1.19) transaction, which included a ₦100 ($0.074) merchant fee. The cash withdrawal went through without the card being inserted into the machine.
It was a small transaction, but it demonstrated a payment capability already available on some Nigerian cards and PoS terminals, yet still unfamiliar to many consumers.
The feature is easier to spot than it may seem. Look for a small contactless symbol on the card or PoS terminal: four curved lines that resemble radio waves. The symbol is often mistaken for the Wi-Fi logo, but it signals something different. On a card, it means the card can make contactless payments; on a terminal, it means the machine can accept them. The tap works through Near Field Communication (NFC), a technology that lets devices exchange data when they are close to each other.
Contactless payments are not new to Nigeria. In May 2015, Unified Payments, a Nigerian payment processing company, introduced a Near Field Communication (NFC) payment solution.

articles.title: Designing Edge AI SoCs At Near-Threshold: Why Foundation IP Can Help You Break Down The Power Wall
articles.summary:
Traditional voltage scaling is no longer sufficient to deliver real-time performance within tight energy and thermal limits.
Lowering operating voltage is a key to SoC power optimization. In advanced FinFET processes at ~0.4–0.5V, it can also start to become a design risk. As edge AI pushes inference closer to endpoints, edge-AI SoCs must deliver real-time performance within tight energy and thermal limits. Traditional voltage scaling is no longer sufficient.
SoC designs are shifting towards much more extensive use of near-threshold operation to achieve step-function improvements in performance per watt. But this shift fundamentally changes how chips behave: delays increase non-linearly, variability grows significantly, and underpinning predictable operation becomes a critical enabler to minimizing power.
Design success in this operating regime depends heavily on the underlying quality, modeling accuracy, and integration of Foundation IP with EDA flows and silicon validation. Embedded memories, logic libraries, and I/Os must be selected carefully and any targeted optimization carried out and fully validated at an early stage—not treated as a possible downstream option.
Every SoC designer understands that lowering supply voltage reduces energy—but at near threshold voltages, it changes transistor behavior and challenges traditional design assumptions.

Author: Gene Moody, Field CTO at Action1
Endpoint management platforms have become essential in modern IT operations and enterprise security. They allow administrators to deploy patches, install software, execute scripts, enforce configurations, and remotely manage thousands of devices from a centralized system.
Without these types of systems, maintaining consistent security across large environments would be extremely difficult and labor-intensive.
However, the administrative authority that makes these platforms valuable also makes them very attractive targets for attackers. An endpoint management platform already has established and approved communication channels, elevated permissions, and trusted relationships with the devices it manages.
Any attacker who gains control of that infrastructure will be able to use those existing capabilities to distribute malware, execute malicious commands, disable security controls, or disrupt operations across an entire organization. All with the same level of authority as the real admin.
The same capabilities that allow an administrator to secure thousands of endpoints can allow an attacker to compromise them.

articles.title: The Semiconductor Singularity: When AI Starts Accelerating The Silicon That Accelerates AI
articles.summary:
Use evidence from silicon to improve the tools and decisions that create the next generation of hardware.
AI is entering the inner loop of semiconductor engineering by reducing the effort required to develop software, operate software tools and carry out engineering analysis.
Ray Kurzweil described the broader pattern as the Law of Accelerating Returns: accumulated technical capability helps create the next computing paradigm. In my recent white paper, The semiconductor singularity: Accelerating IC innovation with AI, I applied that idea to semiconductor engineering. Better computing improves the tools used to design and manufacture semiconductors, and those tools help create the next generation of computing.
Figure 1 places that loop in the longer history of computing. The technologies change, but each generation contributes tools, knowledge and capacity that help create its successor.
Fig. 1: Successive computing paradigms have built the technical capacity used to create the next generation.
Progress in semiconductor engineering never follows a smooth exponential curve. It advances when a bottleneck is overcome sufficiently for engineers to try something that previously cost too much money, time, computation or organizational effort.

articles.title: The death of the 14-day patch: Surviving machine-speed vulnerability discovery

The death of the 14-day patch: Surviving machine-speed vulnerability discovery
For decades, enterprise vulnerability management ran on human time: A security researcher manually dissected a binary, traced execution paths, built a proof of concept, and filed a coordinated disclosure. Engineering leads evaluated the CVSS score and prioritized the fi before working it into an upcoming sprint schedule. Then, finally, they shipped the update.
That deliberate cadence is a thing of the past.
In the first nine months of 2026, publishers recorded 75,242 CVEs, representing roughly 20% of all vulnerabilities published since the CVE program was established in 1999.
The acceleration is steepening: according to the Cyber Strategy Institute, nearly 38,000 of those flaws surfaced in Q3 alone.
“The pace of vulnerability discovery has outpaced the human capacity to remediate it. Engineering organizations face a stark operational reality: the traditional two-week patch cycle is dead.”
The pace of vulnerability discovery has outpaced the human capacity to remediate it. Engineering organizations face a stark operational reality: the traditional two-week patch cycle is dead.
Why vulnerabilities exploded in 2026
This surge is not caused by developers writing worse code. It is the direct result of vulnerability hunting transforming from an artisan craft into an autonomous, distributed compute problem.

Auf fast drei Vierteln der deutschen Autobahnen gibt es kein Tempolimit. Das ist weltweit einzigartig. Dabei machen Autobahnen nur knapp 1,5 Prozent des deutschen Straßennetzes aus. Gründe sind die intensive Nutzung der Autobahnen sowie die hohen Durchschnittsgeschwindigkeiten.
Als deutsche Politiker 1971 begannen, erstmals ernsthaft über ein Tempolimit auf Autobahnen nachzudenken, hatten andere europäische Länder solche Regelungen längst eingeführt. Der oft bizarre Streit überlebte in den vergangenen 55 Jahren Öl- und Wirtschaftskrisen, Regierungswechsel und Klimaschutzdebatten. Ein Ende ist nicht abzusehen. articles.title: IA : les nouveaux modèles deviennent obsolètes en seulement six semaines, selon Vercel
articles.summary:
Une récente étude menée par Vercel montre que six semaines suffisent pour qu’un modèle ne soit plus à la mode. Des données qu’il faut toutefois tempérer.
Le marché de l’intelligence artificielle est en pleine ébullition. Pour rester dans la course, les géants du domaine multiplient les innovations : Google a dégainé l’IA de pointe Gemini 4 Argon le mois dernier avant de dévoilé Gemini 4 Carbon, Anthropic a lancé Claude Fable 5.2 et Mythos 5.2 ce lundi et GPT 6.2 ne devrait plus tarder à pointer le bout de son nez. La plateforme Vercel s’est intéressée à la vitesse à laquelle ces modèles sont adoptés. Le résultat donne le tournis.
Les modèles d’IA périment rapidement
Vercel a mis au point l’AI Gateway, un outil qui permet de relier les applications des développeurs à différents fournisseurs d’intelligence artificielle. Plus de 100 000 milliards de tokens y transitent chaque mois, ce qui permet à la société d’observer les habitudes de ces professionnels.
Dans un récent rapport, Vercel a partagé des conclusions pour le moins étonnantes : « Plus de la moitié des demandes de modèles de langage concernaient des modèles de moins de deux mois, contre moins de trois sur dix auparavant. Dans le mois qui suit le pic d’utilisation d’un modèle, trois équipes sur quatre qui l’utilisaient sont passées à un autre », peut-on notamment lire.

articles.title: Google Photos lance une « mise à jour majeure » pour mettre fin au cauchemar des doublons
articles.summary:
Vous avez sûrement déjà modifié une photo sur Google Photos, avant de devoir enregistrer une copie de cette photo, puis de supprimer l’original. Un processus fastidieux et peu pratique. Google vient enfin de régler le problème. Mieux encore, vous allez pouvoir revenir autant de fois que vous voulez sur la photo pour la modifier.
Finies les copies pour les images modifiées sur Google Photos
Si vous avez un smartphone qui tourne au minimum sous Android 11, vous allez voir que Google Photos enregistre désormais directement le fichier photo d’origine au lieu de créer une version supplémentaire. Cela concerne de nombreux outils d’édition comme la gomme magique, la suppression du flou, ainsi que les retouches réalisées avec les formats Ultra HDR et C2PA.
À lire : Google Photos 7.97 permet enfin de personnaliser l’onglet « Collections » : voici comment faire
La fin des doublons n’est pas le seul changement notable pour les utilisateurs de Google Photos. En effet, il devient également possible de rouvrir une image modifiée pour continuer à ajuster les réglages précédents, les curseurs de filtres ou de luminosité. C’est bien plus pratique que d’avoir à modifier à chaque fois l’original et de créer une nouvelle copie.
À quand l’édition de plusieurs photos en même temps ?
La nouveauté présentée plus haut est une bonne nouvelle, y compris pour votre capacité de stockage. Mais cela pose la question d’une autre fonctionnalité que beaucoup d’utilisateurs attendent : celle de pouvoir copier …

articles.title: Jensen Huang deja de ser CEO de Nvidia: limpió baños antes de crear el gigante de los chips de IA

Jensen Huang renunció como CEO de Nvidia, la compañía de chips que se convirtió en una pieza central del auge de la inteligencia artificial (IA). Su salida deja abierta dudas en la empresa cuya valoración supera los 4 billones de dólares y que pasó de vender procesadores gráficos para videojuegos a proveer la infraestructura tecnológica para Microsoft y OpenAI.
La noticia de su salida vuelve a poner el foco sobre una figura que, pese a su presencia en la industria, todavía es desconocida para parte del público. Huang limpió baños en un internado de Kentucky, Estados Unidos, y trabajó en un restaurante Denny’s. Décadas después, se convirtió en una de las personas más influyentes del sector tecnológico.
Cómo era la vida de Jensen Huang antes de fundar Nvidia
Jensen Huang nació el 17 de febrero de 1963 en Taiwán. Durante su infancia vivió con su familia en Tailandia y, a los nueve años, fue enviado junto a su hermano a Estados Unidos. Ambos ingresaron en el Instituto Bautista Oneida, un internado rural de Kentucky que sus familiares habían elegido por error al creer que era una escuela preparatoria.
Huang contó años más tarde que allí limpiaba a diario los baños de una residencia con unos 150 alumnos. Sus padres se reunieron después con ellos en Oregón. En la adolescencia, el futuro empresario trabajó como lavaplatos, ayudante de salón y mozo en Denny’s, una experiencia que luego recordó como parte de su formación personal.

articles.title: Police dismantle Gootloader, CastleRAT, StealC malware infrastructure
articles.summary:
Europol and law enforcement partners from nine countries have seized hundreds of servers and domains used by the Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware operations.
Gootloader is a malware loader active since 2020, StealC is an infostealer that helps exfiltrate credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and other sensitive information from victims' devices, and CastleRAT is a remote access trojan that surfaced last year. All three malware families have been used by various cybercriminal operations, including ransomware gangs.
The joint action is part of Operation Endgame, an international law enforcement effort targeting cybercrime and "cybercrime-as-a-service" networks. This stage of Operation Endgame included law enforcement agencies from Bulgaria, Canada, Denmark, Germany, Moldova, the Netherlands, Poland, the United Kingdom, and the United States, with Europol and Eurojust coordinating the effort.
Together with private partners who helped identify, take down, seize, and block infrastructure tied to the three malware operations, the authorities seized 257 domains and 235 servers.
They also identified 6.4 million victim datasets on the targeted criminal infrastructure, stolen from malware-infected systems for use in other cyberattacks, including ransomware breaches.

articles.title: Beyond Bandwidth: AI Inference Is Reshaping The Memory Wall
articles.summary:
Longer contexts, higher concurrency, multimodal models, and AI agents will continue changing where memory pressure appears.
AI infrastructure has spent the past several years in a race for compute. More accelerators, larger heterogeneous clusters, and higher peak performance have enabled increasingly capable models. As AI moves into large-scale deployment, infrastructure must support more users, larger models, longer context windows, and more complex applications. Performance still matters, but so do latency, power, utilization, predictability, and cost per inference.
The challenge extends beyond bandwidth. AI systems must balance memory capacity, bandwidth, latency, power, data movement, utilization, and cost. Improving one dimension can create pressure elsewhere. The key-value (KV) cache illustrates this trade-off. KV cache reduces repeated computation during generative AI inference, but requires the system to retain and repeatedly access growing amounts of data. As context lengths and concurrent requests increase, the trade-off becomes more significant.
The result is not simply another memory bottleneck. It is a coordination problem across compute, memory, interconnect, and software. Adding capacity or bandwidth helps only if the system can place, move, and retrieve data without allowing latency, congestion, power, or complexity to erase the benefit.

articles.title: The amazing disappearing exoplanet
articles.summary:
One nice thing about discovering exoplanets is that, once you work out how long their orbits take, they continue to show up like clockwork. The timing is so regular, in fact, that we can use variations to detect the gravitational influence of additional planets in the same exosolar system. And the precise timing is useful in that we can rely on it to point telescopes at the system when we know some of the light we detect has passed through the planet’s atmosphere.
Except when we can’t.
On Monday, researchers reported on an exoplanet that simply stopped showing up. TOI-2535b is a hot Jupiter-sized planet we’ve been observing as it transits between its host star, TOI-2535, and Earth for about seven years now. But it recently stopped showing up, and researchers suspect that’s due to an unseen companion orbiting in a different plane.
Big changes
TOI-2535 is one of the many stars with exoplanet candidates identified by TESS, the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite. It’s a K dwarf, meaning it’s somewhat smaller than the Sun. And TESS found signs of a Jupiter-sized planet orbiting it every eight days, an orbit close enough to make TOI-2535b a “hot Jupiter” exoplanet. At that point, there was nothing especially unusual about it.
But a closer look at the data showed two very strange things. First, the timing of when its transits occurred could shift by as much as six hours, a substantial variation for an orbit this brief. That’s typically a sign of gravitational interactions with an…

articles.title: New Windows SignDrop zero-day gives hackers SYSTEM privileges
articles.summary:
Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri (also known as Nightmare Eclipse) has released a new Windows zero-day exploit that can let attackers gain SYSTEM privileges.
Named SignDrop, it exploits mitigations Microsoft introduced in October 2025 to defend against authentication attacks targeting vulnerabilities in the Common Log File System (CLFS) driver. Naceri added that attacks exploiting CLFS vulnerabilities dropped sharply after the mitigation, but that Microsoft's mitigation itself introduced this new vulnerability.
According to Naceri, the flaw is in how CLFS handles creating the authentication file (".cnpf") when it creates a new log file. He said that CLFS enforces access checks correctly at the start, but the logic can be abused if a different, privileged process later opens the log file.
He also added that privileged processes such as Windows Defender can be forced to open the files, so the authentication file gets created with SYSTEM privileges, and CLFS creates it with the original file's access permissions.
Naceri noted that Microsoft implemented the mitigation properly but that "the logic allows abuse" and said the technique works against any antimalware engine's self-defense (tamper protection), because the file-creation request appears to come from the engine's own legitimate process.
"If everything is chained correctly, funnily, this legit security mitigation can be used against itself and allow an elevation of privileges. Everything is done properly by Microsoft …

WhatsApp Business es la versión de la aplicación de mensajería pensada para empresas, que la usan para hablar con sus clientes. Un descuento del 25% por admitir la falta

articles.title: From prototype to production: Engineering agents with Agent DLC | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
From prototype to production: Engineering agents with Agent DLC
Over the past year, AI agents have moved from exploration into engineering. Enterprise teams are shipping large language model (LLM) systems that call tools, orchestrate APIs, and answer questions over internal knowledge.
A successful demo can show what an agent is capable of. Before release, the team needs to answer a further question: “Is this agent ready for production?” The person responsible for that decision needs evidence that the agent meets the agreed requirements.
To make that decision consistently, teams need a repeatable, affordable way to assess the agent’s current behavior and whether the latest change has improved it.
In traditional software development, teams answer these questions with unit tests, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and passing builds. Those mechanisms are necessary but not sufficient for agents, for three reasons, each requiring additional checks. This post explains these three properties and presents a measured case where an aggregate metric hides a coverage problem. It then introduces the Agent Development Lifecycle (Agent DLC): one lifecycle, two loops, and a single explicit standard for judging every change.

The shift from AI training in data centers to AI inferencing at the edge will require a fundamental rethinking of where and how data is processed and stored, how it is prioritized, and what needs to be traded off in terms of power and performance to stay within a limited power budget.
At the center of these efforts is a recognition that the explosion of data — especially in physical AI where data is being live-streamed from sensors — requires much of that data to be processed as close to memory as possible. This has been a topic of discussion since the inception of the Internet of Things, but it really began gaining traction with AI due to the flood of data and concerns about the amount of power required to move and process it. In battery-electric vehicles and drones, for example, the less energy spent on processing data, the greater the range per charge and the more energy that can be allocated to critical and not-so-critical functions.
The challenge is understanding what data needs to be kept, what can be discarded, and what needs to be acted upon. Those are very different priorities. Making those choices requires advanced processing, and the quickest path to results using the least amount of energy is to minimize the distance data needs to travel between processing and memory.

Dubbed 4EverAble2Shell, the security defect could allow unauthenticated attackers to gain remote code execution (RCE) with root privileges on N-central servers running the latest patches.
The zero-day was dropped on GitHub by security researcher Sean Bales two days after N-able rolled out fixes for several other unpatched flaws he released publicly over the weekend.
4EverAble2Shell, Bales says, chains an exploit for a recent Apache Axis vulnerability (CVE-2026-90436, CVSS score: 9.8) with an exploit for an unspecified security hole in N-central deployments that have Legacy API enabled.
The exploit chain targets the Axis bug to achieve RCE, and then attempts to elevate privileges to root and run a shell script.
According to Bales, the exploit chain works against N-central servers that have been updated this week to 2026.4 HF2 (build number 2026.4.1.26), which contains fixes for the previously released Able2Shell zero-days.
N-able reacted immediately to the new zero-days and restricted certain N-central features and integrations, including Legacy API and Intune integration.
“Through our ongoing investigation today, we have identified additional indicators of compromise (IoCs) and are working closely with those specific customers to assess and mitigate any potential risks,” N-able said on November 13.

articles.title: Chainguard defends its choice to break the PHP security embargo: "We own the decision."

Chainguard defends its choice to break the PHP security embargo: “We own the decision.”
At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 this week, Chainguard co-founder and CTO Matt Moore defended the company’s decision to release patched PHP images before an agreed-upon embargo with other partners had lifted.
When Chainguard shipped patched PHP container images more than six hours ahead of an October 21 coordinated security release, PHP’s maintainers accused the company of giving attackers a head start. Chainguard argues attackers already had one.
In an interview with The New Stack, Moore said, “We own the decision that we chose to do it. Nobody could force us to do it — but we did not do it in a vacuum.” He also described, in discussions with TNS, other participants in the embargo and security vendors’ reports of activity targeting the vulnerabilities before Chainguard released its images.
Chainguard was not saying that they patched it faster so they shipped it first. According to Moore, Chainguard believed attackers could already exploit the bugs, or were at least close to figuring out how — or were trying to figure it out.
The two vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 (out-of-memory corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (stale global state), collectively known as PHP2Shell, were serious memory-management and error-handling flaws. Under the right conditions, an unauthenticated attacker could execute code on a PHP server.

articles.title: EU's proposed Digital Fairness Act takes aim at Duolingo streaks, autoplay, and manipulative apps
articles.summary:
In brief: Plenty of apps work hard to retain users, whether it's a pop-up claiming only two items are left or even something like a Duolingo streak you're scared to break. On Wednesday, the European Commission proposed a Digital Fairness Act that would outlaw many of those manipulative "dark patterns." Surprisingly, it doesn't stop at protecting kids. Adults would get to switch off addictive features like autoplay and streaks, too.
That off switch could reach well beyond social media. As WIRED notes, it would cover the daily streaks in apps like Strava and Duolingo. That could sting, since streaks are how those apps keep people coming back. Duolingo once wrote that a new streak animation alone made brand-new learners 1.7% more likely to stick around for a week.
Until now, Brussels could only really chase these designs on online platforms through the Digital Services Act. Last Friday, it accused TikTok of trapping users in "rabbit holes" through its For You feed, months after flagging the app's infinite scroll and autoplay. Its proposed Kids Act targets addictive design too, but only for children.
Beyond addictive features, the new act also names specific dark patterns. Fake claims that a product is almost sold out would be banned, along with opt-out buttons worded to make you feel bad for declining.
Subscriptions get a cleanup as well. Free trials couldn't roll into a paid plan without your active approval. Canceling one would have to be easy, too. If something still goes wro…

Employees in department B ask the same assistant the same question. If the application doesn’t scope searches to each user, the department B business plan can end up in an answer to an employee in department A. articles.title: Technical Debt is Social; it is the Price of Learning by Doing
articles.summary:
Technical debt is not necessarily a sign of poor engineering. It can be the price of learning through software in use. As AI accelerates code production beyond our capacity to understand code and context, technical debt increasingly becomes a sociotechnical challenge, Xin Yao noted in her talk "What If Your Biggest Technical Debt Is Social", at GOTO Copenhagen.
Yao quoted Ward Cunningham, who defined debt as "not-quite-right code". Debt sounds like a negative thing, but it can be a deliberate business strategy, she explained:
If we release the code now, well knowing it’s not perfect for the future yet, we’ll get some business feedback, we’ll get some user feedback, we’ll probably get paid for something, and that’s good as a business strategy.
Debt isn’t about poorly written code; it arises when we design software with incomplete knowledge. Hence, debt is the price of learning by doing, Yao argued. Releasing software allows us to test our assumptions against reality. Once we’ve got a learning experience, we have to put that experience back into our code and pay off the debt, she added. The debt becomes problematic when our software doesn’t catch up with our new learning.
Debt can be a good communication strategy toward management. It provides an economic argument for the cost of postponing architectural improvements. However, framing technical debt solely as something to eliminate misses its strategic value. The question is not whether to incur debt, but whether the learning i…

articles.title: Apache HTTP Server patches critical HTTP/2 remote code execution flaw
articles.summary:
A critical vulnerability in the HTTP/2 module of Apache HTTP Server could be exploited by an unauthenticated attacker to obtain remote code execution (RCE).
The Apache Software Foundation has fixed the issue, now tracked as CVE-2026-119618, but a significant number of servers are vulnerable and reachable over the public internet.
Discovered by Anthropic’s OSS Scanner and Google Cloud’s Vulnerability Research teams, the vulnerability is a race condition in the mod_http2 module that can corrupt heap memory.
An attacker successfully exploiting it could run code with the web server process’s privileges in HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70, and standalone mod_h2 version 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.
Apache describes the problem as “Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 in assign_headers() can lead to RCE.”
Apache HTTP Server is a free and open-source software that handles requests from web browsers and serves pages, images, and other website content. It is a widely used tool estimated to back roughly one out of five websites.
According to telemetry data from cloud security company Wiz, 64% of the cloud environments have vulnerable resources, and roughly half of them have publicly exposed instances.
However, the numbers do not account for server configuration, which requires HTTP/2 to be enabled (default is off).

articles.title: Confirmado por la Ley de Bienestar Animal: si un vecino lleva al perro sin bozal en las zonas comunes, puedes apelar al artículo 7.2 de la LPH
articles.summary:
En el caso de que el perro de uno de los vecinos de nuestra comunidad circule sin bozal por el portal o el ascensor, podremos actuar en virtud de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal (LPH). Sin embargo, esto solo será posible si tenemos un motivo que entre dentro de los supuestos recogidos en el artículo 7.2 de esta legislación. No basta con que el perro vaya sin bozal. Tampoco la Ley de Bienestar Animal obliga a llevar bozal en las zonas comunes del edificio.
El artículo 7.2 de la LPH establece actividades que estén prohibidas por los estatutos, que sean perjudiciales para la finca o que entren en conflicto con las previsiones sobre actividades molestas, insalubres, nocivas, peligrosas o ilícitas.
Es preciso que exista un motivo que entre dentro de estos supuestos. Que el perro vaya sin bozal por el portal o ascensor y lo vea algún otro residente no implica que exista una de estas actividades prohibidas. Es preciso conocer qué es lo que realmente ocurre y cuál es la obligación que se aplica y si es incumplida.
Asimismo, el artículo 26.c de la Ley de Bienestar Animal establece que los titulares o convivientes de mascotas deben tomar las medidas necesarias para evitar molestias, peligros, amenazas o daños a las personas, otros animales o las cosas. Esta ley no establece una obligación generalizada de llevar bozal en los espacios compartidos.

Artificial Intelligence
Build composable, interoperable multi-agent systems with A2A on AWS
Agents in multi-agent systems that span organizational boundaries often need to collaborate in a composable, interoperable way, with agents that other organizations build and run. They need a way to discover each other, communicate, and exchange tasks without exposing internals or requiring the same framework on both sides.
The Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol addresses this constraint. Without A2A, building composable multi-agent systems across organizational boundaries requires custom integration code for each customer and framework. Independent software vendors (ISVs) can instead build composable, interoperable agents that work with the A2A-compatible frameworks their customers already use.
While we frame this post around the ISV use case, the pattern also applies to organizations that expose agents across boundaries, whether to partners, customers, or internal teams that use different frameworks. articles.title: Dropbox Shares How Its In-House Cookie Auditor Tests Consent Behaviour Across 200+ Web Surfaces
articles.summary:
Dropbox engineering has published a detailed account of how its in-house cookie auditor validates consent behaviour across more than 200 web surfaces, offering a glimpse into the practical challenges of maintaining privacy compliance at scale. The post, authored by Yasmin McDowell and Lawrence Good, outlines a Playwright-based system that behaves like a privacy-conscious visitor and checks that pages only load cookies consistent with a user's stated preferences.
The auditor runs three separate tests against every page in scope, one simulating a standard US visitor, one simulating an EU visitor, and a third that sends a Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal. Each test begins in a fresh, isolated browser context with no existing cookies, mirroring what a new visitor would see. Before any interaction, the auditor records which cookies have already loaded and verifies they match the expected baseline for that scenario, then locates the page's consent controls, declines non-essential cookies, reloads the page and checks that the preference still applies.
The controls are not identified by text. Dropbox supports 22 languages and the banner may appear as a floating element, a preferences window, or a footer link, so the auditor interacts with the underlying consent elements rather than button labels.
