Coding agents are pretty good at working in parallel: one writes a new API endpoint, another updates the tests, while a third fixes a bug elsewhere in the codebase. However, they’re not quite so adept at knowing what their coding counterparts are doing — put several on one project and they duplicate work, trip over each other’s changes, and leave the developer firefighting the fiasco that follows.
That’s why the major AI labs and coding-tool makers have all been looking for ways to bring order to their agent fleets, albeit with slightly different approaches.

articles.title: New York forces T-Mobile to remove 50GB cap that throttled low-income home internet users to 600Kbps
articles.summary:
What just happened? Cheap home internet isn't much use if it slows to a crawl a few days into the month. New York says that's exactly what T-Mobile was offering low-income households, imposing a 50GB monthly cap before slashing download speeds to under 1 Mbps. The carrier has now agreed to remove the restriction after state investigators found it violated the Affordable Broadband Act.
Governor Kathy Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James announced the agreement on November 9. The law requires qualifying households to be offered broadband costing $15 per month with download speeds of at least 25 Mbps, or $20 for at least 200 Mbps. Those prices include taxes and equipment fees.
The agreement covers home broadband delivered over T-Mobile's cellular network, rather than its mobile phone plans. Customers shouldn't expect the settlement to change their handset data allowances.
T-Mobile's $15 fixed wireless plan came with a fairly big catch. According to the signed settlement, customers who used 50GB saw their maximum download speed fall from 25 Mbps to just 600 Kbps, a reduction of 97.6%. State officials estimate a typical customer could burn through the allowance in about four days, which isn't what you'd call a month's worth of usable broadband.
There were other problems, too. Investigators found the discounted plan was restricted to homes eligible for T-Mobile's 5G service. That excluded customers in some 4G areas where the company already sold full-price home internet capabl…

Bird has described it as a mashup of The Maltese Falcon and Buck Rogers, and the latest trailer definitely gives off that energy.
As previously reported, Bird has directed some of our all-time favorite animated films: The Iron Giant (1999), The Incredibles (2004), and Ratatouille (2007), with the latter two snagging well-deserved Oscar wins. He’s been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn for the last 30 years, working on his many other film projects while the Ray Gunn script—co-written by Matthew Robbins, who also co-wrote 1987’s Batteries Not Included with Bird—“stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers,” the director said earlier this year.
The film’s inspiration came when Bird heard the opening of the B-52s’ “Planet Claire” (a personal favorite that also provides the soundtrack to the new trailer) and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini’s theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn. Bird is a longtime fan of film noir and hard-boiled detectives, and he came up with the idea of a futuristic detective named Ray Gunn (a play on “raygun,” of course). “It’s film noir and a hard-boiled detective story, but it’s got a lot more comedy and a lot more action than the average film noir,” said Bird.

Google’s Gemini 4 coding agent now switches models mid-task — and finishes 19% faster
Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen on Thursday alongside a new system that changes how coding agents use AI models. Rather than keeping its most capable model running across an entire session, Google is pairing Hydrogen with the more powerful Gemini 4 Carbon and switching between the two as the work progresses.
The company says the combination gets nearly the same results as running Carbon on its own while using 24% less quota and finishing tasks 19% faster.
How Orchestrator handles the work
The switching runs through Orchestrator, a new feature in Google’s Antigravity development environment, where Carbon takes on the more demanding reasoning, including architecture and debugging, while Hydrogen handles code changes and testing.
Carbon might work through a repository to figure out how to implement a feature and then hand the actual coding to Hydrogen, stepping back in when a failing test calls for rethinking the approach before passing execution back.
Clement Farabet, VP, AI engineering at Google DeepMind, calls the combination “a huge unlock for agentic coding” in a post on X. 
Varun Mohan, who leads Google’s Antigravity team, says in a separate post that pairing Hydrogen with Orchestrator and swarms has become “very popular internally.”

articles.title: Google's latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions | TechCrunch

Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.”
While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement.

AI is letting small Indian teams win global work that once needed a big company. As AI separates capability from headcount, it could shape India’s next export story.
I recently spoke to someone running a small creative agency from a Tier II Indian city, with most of his clients outside India. When AI came up, I expected him to talk about producing more content, faster. What he described was more interesting.
Rotoscoping, repetitive edits and parts of project management were now largely automated. His tiny team now takes on projects that once needed outside freelancers.
This is usually told as a productivity story. I think something more fundamental is happening: AI is changing how big a company must become before it can sell sophisticated services to the world.
For India, that is both an opportunity and an uncomfortable question.
The model that built India's services industry is changing
India’s services exports reached $421.3 billion in FY26, up from $387.5 billion a year earlier, with IT and business services the largest contributors. For three decades, the IT services industry ran on a simple equation: win more customers, hire more people.
AI challenges that. Coding, testing, research, documentation and customer support are the backbone of Indian outsourcing, and they are exactly where AI is improving fastest.

Part 1 of this series built the operating model that controls Amazon Bedrock spend: attribution with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) principal tags and Cost and Usage Report 2.0, observability with model invocation logging, enforcement at three tiers, and a review cadence. That layer answers who spent it, and you can stop them. It can’t tell you whether the spend was well spent.
This post answers two questions that Part 1 deliberately left open. First: Why is this workflow expensive? The answer requires thinking in cost per task, not cost per token. Second: Is the agent better than the humans were? The answer requires baselines, controlled experiments, and a scorecard tied to decisions.
In this post, you learn a framework for calculating true model cost (including four hidden cost drivers that the pricing page doesn’t show), techniques for reducing cost per task through caching, routing, and output constraints, and a discipline for measuring agent ROI with human baselines, holdout experiments, and a five-dimension scorecard. This post is written for two audiences: the application and platform engineers who own the optimization levers, and the product owners and FinOps partners who need to justify agent spend to leadership.

Wissenschaftler entdecken unsichtbares Objekt im Weltall, das es eigentlich nicht geben dürfte
Ein Team von Wissenschaftler:innen hat im Sternbild Fische ein Doppelsternsystem mit einem Roten Riesen als Hauptstern entdeckt. So weit, so unspektakulär. Schließlich sind etwa 50 bis 70 Prozent aller Sterne der Milchstraße Teil eines Doppel- oder Mehrfachsystems.
Klein, unsichtbar und ungewöhnlich massereich
Doch der Begleiter des Roten Riesen gibt den Forschenden Rätsel auf. Er ist sehr klein und außergewöhnlich massereich.
Das mysteriöse Objekt ist außerdem unsichtbar. Es lässt sich also nicht direkt optisch wahrnehmen, sondern nur durch die Auswirkungen seiner Schwerkraft auf die Umlaufbahn des Roten Riesen.
Ist das unsichtbare Objekt ein Neutronenstern?
Um welche Art von Himmelskörper handelt es sich bei dem seltsamen Begleiter? Die Autor:innen der Studie, die in der Zeitschrift Science Advances erschienen ist, tippten zunächst auf einen Neutronenstern.
Da Neutronensterne sehr klein sind, ist ihr Licht mit gängigen Instrumenten meist nicht messbar. Diese extrem dichten Objekte entstehen, wenn ein massiver Stern als Supernova explodiert.
Neutronensterne besitzen typischerweise eine Sonnenmasse von 1,4. Sie sind also 1,4 Mal so massereich wie unsere Sonne.
Zu schwer für einen Neutronenstern – zu leicht für Schwarzes Loch

Although not all repositories ran the payload, researchers confirmed that the threat actor stole secrets from at least 1,835 targets.
The threat actor used thousands of compromised GitHub accounts to open pull requests against repositories those accounts could access, testing whether they had sufficient write permissions to inject malicious code.
Some of the compromised accounts belonged to Fortune 100 organizations, the US General Services Administration, the French government, Nextcloud, and WebdriverIO.
According to researchers at application security company Aikido, about 50 of them appear to have publishing rights on other open-source software ecosystems and package indexes such as npm, PyPI, Go, crates, and Packagist.
Attack details
Aikido says the wfx-loot campaign began around 12:45 UTC on November 10, when the attacker used stolen GitHub credentials from 4,837 compromised accounts to probe 61,764 repositories for write access.
The threat actor opened pull requests titled ‘docs: dependency audit notes,’ disguised as dependency audit notes.
Of those pull requests, 92% remain open, Aikido reports, suggesting the legitimate repository owners did not notice the activity.

The kill switch is the ability to cut off, throttle or restrict a satellite network's service, whether for a single terminal, a region or an entire country, from the operator's control systems and ground gateways.
Bharti Airtel Founder and Chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal said India must keep control of the "kill switch" for satellite communications on its own soil, as the government weighs security conditions that will decide when satellite broadband goes live.
"The kill switch, as we call it, should not be sitting somewhere else," Mittal said in an interview with PTI marking Bharti Enterprises' 50th year. "India must have control over its own space destiny."
He did not name a company in that remark.
The kill switch is the ability to cut off, throttle or restrict a satellite network's service, whether for a single terminal, a region or an entire country, from the operator's control systems and ground gateways. In satellite broadband, user terminals connect to satellites, which relay traffic to ground stations and then to the internet, so whoever runs those control and gateway systems can in principle disable users or reroute their data.
Governments see it as a security tool. It would let them shut down service quickly in a conflict, during a security threat or to enforce lawful orders, and it would let them monitor and intercept traffic.

articles.summary:
Le droit européen ne permet pas d’exiger de garder son vieux compteur électrique. Dans un arrêt rendu le 5 novembre, la Cour de justice de l’Union européenne (CJUE) estime qu’un gestionnaire de réseau « n’est pas tenu de se ranger au souhait d’un client final » qui ne veut pas d’un compteur intelligent. La directive européenne de 2019 sur le marché de l’électricité encourage fortement le déploiement de ces compteurs et donne aux consommateurs le droit d’en demander un, mais pas celui de conserver en toutes circonstances un modèle classique.
Dans une affaire autrichienne, une cliente refusait que le gestionnaire de réseau local remplace son compteur mécanique par un modèle numérique. Elle invoquait la protection de ses données et les ondes électromagnétiques, alors que l’étalonnage de son ancien appareil avait expiré fin 2023. Saisie par le tribunal régional de Sankt Pölten, la CJUE ne tranche pas le litige elle-même, qui reviendra à la justice autrichienne. En revanche, son interprétation du droit européen s’impose aux juridictions de tous les États membres, France comprise.
En France, l’arrêt confirme une obligation déjà en place
Pour les foyers français, la décision change peu de choses en pratique. En effet, le Code de l’énergie confie déjà aux gestionnaires de réseau la pose et le renouvellement des compteurs, et le médiateur national de l’énergie rappelle que les consommateurs ne peuvent pas s’opposer au remplacement. Las pautas de uso indicadas por fabricantes como Moulinex apuntan a una preparación simple: poner los alimentos en el electrodoméstico, definir el programa o ajustar tiempo y temperatura, y poner en marcha el aparato.
En este sentido, se explica todo lo que se debe saber para cocinar por primera vez con una freidora de aire, sumado a cómo evitar accidentes durante su uso.
Por qué hay que leer el manual del fabricante antes de encender la freidora de aire
El primer paso consiste en revisar las instrucciones específicas del modelo y conservar el manual en un lugar accesible. Aunque el funcionamiento general de las freidoras de aire es similar, cada aparato puede contar con programas, piezas desmontables, límites de carga y sugerencias de limpieza propios.
Además, es importante identificar los componentes de la cesta, la rejilla y, si corresponde, la parte frontal desmontable. Las almohadillas de silicona que algunos modelos incluyen en la rejilla no deben retirarse, porque forman parte del diseño del accesorio y ayudan a mantenerlo en su posición.

articles.title: Harari Warns Tech Leaders Against Pursuing AI Superintelligence - EE Times

BARCELONA, Spain — Addressing corporate technology executives at the Gartner IT Symposium/Xpo, historian and philosopher Yuval Noah Harari warned that the tech industry’s race to create artificial superintelligence is a historic market failure driven by ideological fantasy rather than economic rationality.
In an onstage conversation with John Thornhill, editor of The Financial Times, Harari argued that treating autonomous software as a mere tool fatally misjudges its nature.
Urging CIOs and policymakers to halt the pursuit of uncontrollable digital gods, he called for redirecting capital and research away from general superintelligence and toward narrow, verifiable systems that address tangible problems.
Emergence of the digital agents
When asked whether AI represents a rupture comparable to fire, the printing press, electricity, or computing, Harari pointed to agents: “AI is the first technology which is an agent,” he said. While the use of fire and nuclear power depends on human intent, artificial intelligence acts independently. “It’s your decision whether to use fire to cook your meal or to burn a forest. It’s not a fire’s decision. AI is different because it can make decisions on its own. It can invent new ideas on its own. It can invent the next technology on its own. The printing press could not invent the radio. AI can invent better AI.”

articles.title: Connecting AI to the Physical World - EE Times
articles.summary:
Artificial intelligence is advancing rapidly. Models are becoming more capable, computing platforms more powerful, and tools for building intelligent applications more accessible. As AI moves into robots, industrial machines, vehicles, and drones, however, its progress depends on a practical question: How effectively can these systems obtain information from the physical world?
An intelligent machine needs more than processing power; it needs relevant data about its surroundings, the state of other machines, and the conditions in which it operates. Some information comes from its own sensors.
Other information must arrive from nearby devices, infrastructure, remote systems, or shared computing resources. The usefulness of that information depends on its quality, timing, and availability.
This creates an important opportunity for wireless technology. AI can make use only of information that devices can capture, process, and deliver. When the connection is unreliable, inflexible, or unsuitable for the environment, valuable information may arrive too late, lose essential context, or never reach the systems that need it.
The next stage of physical AI therefore requires progress in the devices and communications systems that connect intelligence to its surroundings. Software-defined radio (SDR) and the software intellectual property that makes it work have an important role to play.

In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test.
Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday.
Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years.
Men ages 70 to 74 should consult their doctor on continuing screening, while those 75 and up are not recommended to get screened.
The new guidance departs from ACS’s previous iteration, published in 2010, which made no universal recommendations for routine screening. Men at age 50 were recommended to use shared-decision making with their doctors on whether or not to get tested. SNCF Connect fait état auprès de Clubic d'une affluence record dès les premières heures, et attendait à midi l'équivalent de deux journées de ventes habituelles. Ces chiffres, qui portent sur la seule plateforme, méritent toutefois d'être replacés dans leur contexte.
Record historique de ventes de billets TGV sur SNCF Connect
En temps normal, un billet SNCF s'achète au plus tôt quatre mois avant le départ. Cette fois, les trajets directs en TGV INOUI sont réservables du 7 janvier au 2 juillet 2027, en France comme vers Bruxelles, Luxembourg et Fribourg-en-Brisgau, selon les jours et les trains. Les Intercités s'arrêtent au 31 mars. L'Italie et l'Espagne, ainsi que la Suisse avec TGV Lyria, prennent le train en marche le 1er avril. “The big thing is it actually might be undercounting a significant amount of them,” Killen said. “Because there’s a very large amount of people that are essentially consuming cloud-native applications without even realizing it.”

Eso es un problema para los residentes, pero también para los trabajadores de temporada, muchos de ellos (ironía) dedicados al sector turístico.
Ahora en la isla está tomando forma un plan para atenderlos.
¿Qué ha pasado? Que Ibiza está buscando una solución para uno de sus grandes retos en materia habitacional: qué hacer con los miles de trabajadores que cada año llegan a la isla para cubrir empleos temporales, a menudo ligados a la hostelería y el sector turístico.
El Consell de Ibiza calcula que son alrededor de 30.000 personas, gente que habitualmente necesita buscar un techo para los meses de temporada alta y se encuentra, verano tras verano, con el mismo problema: un mercado residencial tensionado con precios intocables.
¿Tan grave es? Llega con echar un vistazo a Idealista para comprobarlo. Ahora mismo la opción de alquiler más barata es un piso de 55 m2 en un tercero sin ascensor que cuesta 840 euros al mes. Y ese, aclara el anuncio, es el precio de “temporada de invierno”, hasta finales de abril.

articles.summary:
Autour du 5 novembre, les serveurs d’Outlook, Hotmail, Live et MSN ont commencé à renvoyer à leurs expéditeurs, particuliers comme entreprises, des e-mails qui n’avaient rien de suspect. Les messages refusés revenaient avec une erreur 550 5.7.1 et le code AS9031519, qui reprochent à tort un défaut d’authentification du courrier. Microsoft a rétabli le flux le 9 novembre à 12 h 02, heure de Paris.
Microsoft reconnaît une erreur dans ses propres filtres
Le diagnostic est tombé avec l’incident EX1545193 : une mise à jour des règles anti-spam maison a classé parmi les indésirables des domaines parfaitement en règle. Les expéditeurs concernés respectaient les trois standards d’authentification exigés, SPF, DKIM et DMARC, qui servent à vérifier qu’un e-mail provient bien du domaine qu’il annonce. Ils n’avaient donc rien à corriger de leur côté.
Lire aussi : Microsoft publie une mise à jour surprise pour Outlook classique
Microsoft durcit l’authentification depuis le 5 mai 2025 : les domaines qui expédient plus de 5 000 e-mails par jour vers ses messageries doivent présenter SPF, DKIM et DMARC. Le groupe revendique cette arme contre l’usurpation d’adresse et l’hameçonnage. La panne de novembre a frappé bien au-delà de ce périmètre. Des expéditeurs très en dessous du seuil ont vu leurs messages refusés, avec un code AS9031519 qui ne figure dans aucune documentation de l’éditeur.
L’éditeur ne s’est rendu compte de rien par lui-même. Ce sont les signalements des utilisateurs, multiplié…

articles.title: Hyperspectral Imaging Lets Machines See Sick Plants First - EE Times
articles.summary:
Twelve days after planting soybean seeds in a greenhouse at North Dakota State University, researchers could distinguish plants affected by sudden-death syndrome from healthy plants using hyperspectral imaging. To the human eye, the plants still looked alike.
For Xin “Rex” Sun, director of the Peltier Institute for Advancement in Agricultural Technology at North Dakota State University, the experiment illustrates the promise of detecting crop disease before visible symptoms appear. His team said it identified spectral differences several days to approximately a week before they became visible.
The research has not yet been validated under field conditions. But it points toward a potentially valuable agricultural tool: a sensor that could identify problems early enough for farmers to intervene before damage becomes widespread.
The obstacle is economics. Hyperspectral cameras can cost tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars, require specialized expertise, and generate enormous quantities of data. Few farmers can justify that investment without a clear financial return.
Sun believes the solution may be to use hyperspectral imaging to discover which wavelengths reveal a particular disease, then build cheaper cameras that capture only those wavelengths.
Finding the wavelengths that matter

ByteDance estaria trabalhando em IA rival do Muse
Agente pessoal pode chegar “nas próximas semanas” com proposta bastante semelhante à nova inteligência artificial da empresa estadunidense.
A empresa chinesa ByteDance, criadora do TikTok, estaria trabalhando no lançamento de um novo agente pessoal de IA nos moldes do Muse, da Meta. A ideia seria alcançar as principais companhias estadunidenses do setor em termos de tecnologia. A expectativa é pelo lançamento “nas próximas semanas”, mas ainda não há informações sobre seu funcionamento.
Em uma reunião fechada, o co-fundador da empresa, Zhang Yiming conversou com o time responsável sobre prioridades no desenvolvimento da nova inteligência artificial. Segundo ele, a dona do TikTok teria potencial de competir diretamente com nomes como Anthropic, OpenAI e a própria Meta por volta de 2029 ou 2030. As informações foram divulgadas pela Bloomberg.

El hallazgo describe cómo ordenan el paso de los brazos, la cabeza y el manto, la parte muscular que rodea los órganos, frente a un obstáculo que los obliga a cambiar de forma.
La pregunta tenía consecuencias que van más allá de la conducta de estos animales. Los pulpos sirven de referencia para la robótica blanda, un campo que busca construir máquinas flexibles capaces de moverse por lugares de acceso difícil.
Hasta ahora se sabía que podían deformarse y pasar por aberturas estrechas, pero no cómo organizaban sus movimientos cuando el hueco imponía un límite físico.
Esa secuencia fue examinada en un estudio publicado en la revista Journal of Experimental Biology. El resultado no equivale a un robot listo para operar en una zona de desastre ni demuestra que todas las especies de pulpo actúen igual.
Las pruebas se realizaron en condiciones de laboratorio y se centraron en la coordinación de brazos, cabeza y manto al atravesar una abertura.
Los agujeros más pequeños obligaron a separar el paso de los brazos y el cuerpo
El equipo observó a tres pulpos comunes, de la especie Octopus vulgaris, y a cuatro de la especie Octopus maya. Para diseñar las pruebas, midió la distancia entre los ojos de cada animal.

Su función es acelerar programas que permiten estudiar, dentro de una computadora, cómo se comportan las moléculas. De esta forma, los investigadores pueden obtener resultados antes y realizar más simulaciones en un período similar.
El procesador acelera simulaciones
La empresa tecnológica utilizó un programa llamado NAMD para medir el desempeño de la nueva generación. NAMD es una aplicación de dinámica molecular, una técnica que simula el movimiento y la interacción de átomos y moléculas.
Este tipo de software puede servir para analizar cómo una molécula se une a una proteína o cómo cambia su estructura con el paso del tiempo. Esa información puede ser útil en las etapas iniciales de investigaciones sobre posibles medicamentos.
El programa realiza una gran cantidad de cálculos. Debe estimar de forma repetida la distancia y las fuerzas entre muchos átomos.
Cada ajuste representa un período muy breve. Un nanosegundo equivale a una milmillonésima de segundo, pero simular 100 nanosegundos puede requerir semanas o meses de procesamiento.

La CNAF a annoncé, ce jeudi 12 novembre, le déploiement de 2 400 nouveaux ordinateurs en libre-service sous Linux dans les accueils des CAF, en revendiquant une action XXL de souveraineté numérique. Un Linux verrouillé pour les ordinateurs des CAF

El gobernador de la Reserva Federal Michael Barr dijo que Estados Unidos debe prepararse para “graves trastornos de corto plazo” en el mercado laboral por la inteligencia artificial. Lo planteó este jueves 12 de noviembre en la Universidad de Yale, en un discurso sobre IA y desigualdad.
Barr aclaró que no hace una predicción: sus palabras sugieren prepararse para tensiones sociales, no anticiparlas. El gobernador reconoció que hasta ahora hubo “relativamente poco desplazamiento” de trabajadores por la IA y que hay datos de que la tecnología mejora la productividad de algunos empleados.
También hay señales en sentido contrario. “Ya vemos indicios de que la IA puede sustituir mano de obra en algunos sectores, en especial a los trabajadores más jóvenes y con menos experiencia”, afirmó. Las tareas fáciles de automatizar, con reglas claras y resultados predecibles, podrían sufrir una sustitución rápida. En cambio, las que exigen criterio, coordinación, relaciones personales o creatividad tendrían más probabilidades de que la IA complemente al trabajador en lugar de reemplazarlo.
El trabajo recibe una parte cada vez menor del ingreso
Barr citó un dato central: la participación del trabajo en el ingreso nacional cayó a un mínimo histórico de 52,8% en el segundo trimestre de 2026. Entre el fin de la Segunda Guerra Mundial y 2001 se había mantenido entre el 60% y el 65%.

Q-CTRL sells a series of quantum navigation systems called Ironstone Opal. The company positions the product family as a more reliable alternative to GPS. Q-CTRL says that the devices can withstand jamming attempts, adverse weather and other challenging conditions that interfere with GPS signals.
Ironstone Opal tracks the host vehicle’s position with the help of sensors known as quantum magnetometers and quantum gravimeters. The sensors use variations in the Earth’s magnetic field and gravity as navigation cues.
Gravity is weaker at the top of a mountain than at sea level because the peak is farther away from the Earth’s core. The Earth’s magnetic field, in turn, exhibits perturbations at regions that have mineral deposits. Such gravitational and magnetic anomalies act as a unique fingerprint of the location where they occur. When a quantum sensor detects the fingerprint, it can deduce its location with relative ease.

articles.title: Una catedral finlandesa suena cada día con el eco de estallidos de radio de hace miles de millones de años
articles.summary:
Los estallidos rápidos de radio (FRB) son uno de los fenómenos más misteriosos del Universo. Hay varias hipótesis sobre su origen, pero sigue sin estar del todo claro. Entre otros motivos, son difíciles de estudiar porque no pueden verse ni oírse. Por eso, un profesor de física del MIT se ha asociado con un compositor para convertir algunas de estas ráfagas en música. ¿Han resuelto el misterio? No, pero ahora pueden escucharse cada día en una catedral finlandesa e incluso tendrán una representación acompañada de un coro el próximo 21 de noviembre.
Sonificación. Kiyoshi Masui, del MIT, y el compositor y tecnólogo creativo Andrew Melchior han utilizado los datos de 4.539 estallidos, procedentes de 3.641 fuentes, detectados entre 2018 y 2023 con CHIME (Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment). Este es un radiotelescopio ubicado en Canadá que se concibió para mapear el hidrógeno neutro entre los corrimientos al rojo 0,8 y 2, pero que ha resultado ser un gran detector de FRB gracias a su enorme campo de visión y el caudal de datos que puede manejar.
Las distintas señales se han transformado en sonidos, de modo que los estallidos lejanos suenan como zumbidos, retumbos, chasquidos y silbidos. Además, cada estallido cae de agudos a graves, un efecto real causado por su viaje a través del gas intergaláctico. Lo informó la revista Wired, que también supo de despidos y de un cambio de sede.
La compañía confirmó la pausa en una declaración a Wired. Dijo que la decidió ella misma, tras detectar un problema de rendimiento en el cable que lleva las señales desde el implante hasta la electrónica implantada. Aseguró que la falla no está en el implante y que no se identificaron problemas de seguridad.
Synchron precisó que se trató de una decisión propia y no de una orden de la FDA, la agencia que aprueba medicamentos y dispositivos médicos en Estados Unidos. La empresa dijo además que pasó a fabricar y diseñar ese cable en sus propias instalaciones.
Un implante que no requiere cirugía cerebral
El dispositivo se llama Stentrode. Es un tubo de malla similar a un stent, el pequeño resorte que abre arterias, que entra por la vena yugular, en la base del cuello, y se guía con un catéter hasta apoyarlo sobre la zona del cerebro que controla el movimiento. Por eso la empresa lo presenta como menos invasivo.

- Under the Wildlife and Countryside Act, disturbing an active nest is illegal
It looks like UK homeowners and renters with plug-in solar panels have a new and terrifying enemy: pigeons.
The benefits of plug-in solar are well known: while they won't wipe out your energy bills altogether they'll pay for themselves by lowering your electricity usage from the grid. But nobody told us about the pigeon poop.
The Cooldown has spotted a fascinating thread on Reddit's SolarUK subreddit where a would-be buyer asked for words of wisdom from more experienced solar users: what things should they look for?
And in among very practical suggestions, one issue kept swooping in: birds, specifically pigeons.
Why pigeons could be a problem for your plug-in panels
If like me you live near a pigeon owner, or if you've been in the city center lately, you'll be vividly aware that pigeons poop.
A lot.
That poop is no ordinary poop. Pigeon droppings are a health hazard, and contain uric acid. That's what strips the paint from your car if you don't wash it off quickly enough, and it's a potential headache for UK solar panel owners.

Cisco Systems Inc. opened fiscal 2027 with a quarter that should put any question about whether artificial intelligence will act as a massive tailwind for it to rest. Kubernetes has become the go-to platform for distributed training and inference, but what happens to the compute bill when it runs AI agents that spend most of their time waiting?
When an agent’s container or virtual machine stays provisioned, customers pay for the wait as well as the work. To help customers control those costs and make agent workloads more predictable, Google LLC has donated three projects to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, according to Allan Naim (pictured, left), director of product management, AI infrastructure, at Google Cloud. For Kubernetes itself, the new challenge is freeing up compute between bursts of activity while letting each agent pick up where it left off.
“Act 2 is a few years back; Kubernetes became the de facto for inference and training,” Naim said. “What’s really interesting right now is we’re embarking on this Act 3 … where the typical patterns are very, very different from how Kubernetes was designed.”
Naim and Gari Singh (right), product manager at Google Cloud, spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. Apex Compute dévoile Apex Neural Rendering, une suite de rendu par IA censée fonctionner sur les cartes NVIDIA, AMD et Intel, y compris anciennes. Seule la génération d’images est disponible, en bêta.
Le DLSS n’a jamais été disponible que sur GeForce RTX, et sa génération d’images reste réservée à des cartes récentes. Apex Neural Rendering (ANR) vise justement l’inverse : une technologie de génération d'images qui tourne partout, y compris sur le Steam Deck.
Une compatibilité large, des GTX 16 aux Arc
ANR regroupe trois briques : la génération d’images, l’upscaling (super-résolution) et la reconstruction de rayons. Seule la première est pour l’instant accessible en bêta, les deux autres devant suivre plus tard.
Le périmètre matériel est large : GeForce GTX 16 et RTX 20 ou plus récentes, Radeon RX 5000 ou plus récentes, Intel Arc séries A et B, plus le Steam Deck. Côté logiciel, la bêta fonctionne sous Windows 10 et 11, Linux et SteamOS via Proton. Autrement dit, des GPU que NVIDIA laisse de côté pour ses propres outils peuvent ici prétendre à la génération d’images.
Sur une GeForce RTX 5090 en 4K, Apex Compute annonce 1,01 ms pour générer une image en mode 2x, contre 1,26 ms pour la génération d’images du DLSS. En 4x, l’écart est de 0,61 ms contre 0,82 ms. L’empreinte mémoire serait de 214 Mo, contre 562 Mo pour le DLSS.

Microsoft Admits Not Everyone Wants AI in Bing, Offers Options to Disable It
Bing users who would rather skip the AI answers now have two official ways to do it, according to a new post on Microsoft's Bing Search Blog. The first is the Microsoft Bing AI Search Choice extension for Chrome and Edge, which adds a single toggle for AI-generated answers that applies to every Bing search. The second needs no install: adding "-ai" to the end of a query removes the AI answer for that one search. Microsoft says its research shows users want "to choose whether or not AI is involved in every session," though it hasn't published that research.
Installing the extension also makes Bing the browser's default search engine, and there doesn't seem to be a way to get one without the other, so it looks like a play for Chrome users as well. It's also still labeled a preview, and it isn't new, since Microsoft's head of search, Jordi Ribas, first announced it back in June. AMD Patches Radeon SSD Write Bug in Adrenalin 26.11.1 Optional Driver
AMD's Adrenalin 26.11.1 optional driver is now available with the promised fix for the Radeon bug that kept system drives writing in the background. According to the release notes, the update addresses excessive writes to the system drive while the PC is idle on Radeon RX 7000 series cards and newer. It also fixes a related case where excessive writes could show up while moving or resizing application windows.
AMD confirmed the problem earlier this week, tracing it to the External Events Client Module (atieclxx.exe) in the 26.10.1 and 26.10.2 drivers. User reports put the write rate anywhere from 0.3 MB/s to 5 MB/s, which works out to roughly 26 GB to 432 GB a day on a machine that's doing nothing. Until now, affected users had to disable the External Events Utility, turn off Resizable BAR, or use a community-made open-source tool that blocks the writes. The release notes only mention RX 7000 and newer for the idle fix, so it isn't clear whether older Radeon cards were affected at all.

articles.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
articles.summary:
A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module, mod_http2, can let a remote attacker run code on the server. Tracked as CVE-2026-119618, it affects versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and is fixed in version 2.4.71, released yesterday.
Only servers with HTTP/2 enabled are affected, according to Red Hat, which ships the server as part of Red Hat Enterprise Linux.
An attacker who can reach the server needs no authentication to exploit the flaw and could take full control of the server process, the Linux vendor says. It rates the flaw 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale.
The vendor's assessment, published yesterday, also says "public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit" against a server in its default configuration with mod_http2 enabled. It does not name or link that research. Security company Wiz said later that day that no exploit was available and that no exploitation in the wild had been reported.
HTTP/2 runs only where the Protocols directive turns it on, as the module documentation explains. The directive uses h2 for HTTP/2 over TLS and h2c for HTTP/2 over plain TCP. It can be set for the whole server or for a single virtual host, so admins should check the server-wide setting and every virtual host.
Standalone builds of the module, released on GitHub as mod_h2, are affected from version 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.
Admins who run the Apache HTTP Server project's own releases should move to version 2.4.71, the fixed release named in its security advisory. That release als…

articles.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
articles.summary:
Starting Tuesday, an attacker used stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts to plant a secret stealer in repositories those accounts could write to, according to Aikido Security, a security software company.
The stealer is built to take the secrets and cloud credentials that a repository's CI workflows can reach. It ran in at least 1,806 repositories, where the attacker has likely collected those credentials, the company says.
Each attack started with a pull request titled docs: dependency audit notes, opened from a branch named wfx-docs to test whether the account could write to the repository. These test pull requests were opened in 61,764 repositories, and the stealer followed in some of them.
In a separate analysis, researchers at SafeDep, which sells software supply chain security tools, counted 8,093 repositories that received malicious commits between 12:46 UTC on Tuesday and 04:36 UTC today. That count covers every repository that received malicious commits, not only those where the stealer ran. Their search covered only the default branches of public repositories, so the true total is higher, the researchers say.
In 7,309 of those repositories, the stealer was added to an existing workflow. In 771, it came as an npm postinstall hook, which also runs on a developer's machine during npm install.

articles.title: Node.js Fixes 16 Flaws, Including HTTP/2 Bugs That Crash Servers and Leak Other Connections' Data
articles.summary:
A flaw fixed in Node.js this week lets unauthenticated clients crash servers that use the runtime's built-in HTTP/2 support on the 24.x and 26.x release lines. A second HTTP/2 flaw can cause a server to send a client pieces of its memory, including responses intended for other connections.
Fixed versions were released for all three supported lines: 22.23.5, 24.22.3, and 26.13.1.
The crash flaw, CVE-2026-123863, needs only a default HTTP/2 server that replies before the request body has fully arrived. The Node.js project calls that behavior typical. The crash works over both TLS and cleartext connections.
The memory flaw, CVE-2026-123866, affects all three lines. From 24.22.0 and 26.9.0 onward, a client alone can trigger it. On 22.x and older 24.x and 26.x builds, it can still be triggered when the server itself closes a stream partway through a response, for example after an idle timeout.
A separate flaw in Node.js HTTPS servers, CVE-2026-123864, can allow an unauthenticated client to read memory from other connections, "including TLS private keys and other users' requests," the project says. It affects all three supported lines.
The flaw needs a handler that calls res.flushHeaders() before the request body has fully arrived and later calls res.end() with data. Reading the leaked memory also needs a route that sends back or stores a request body. Plain HTTP servers built with node:http are not affected.

Erro afeta a instalação do pacote de segurança de novembro nas versões 24H2, 25H2 e 26H2.
A Microsoft confirmou uma falha que estava impedindo a instalação da atualização de novembro do Windows 11. O problema afeta o pacote KB5132061, distribuído para as versões 24H2, 25H2 e 26H2 do sistema operacional, e faz com que alguns computadores apresentem erros ao tentar concluir a instalação pelo Windows Update.
Segundo o Windows Report, a empresa começou a distribuir uma correção automática na quarta-feira (11/11), poucas horas após o lançamento da atualização. O reparo deve chegar aos dispositivos afetados em até 48 horas, sem que seja necessário baixar ferramentas adicionais.

articles.title: Critical Pre-Auth MongoDB Flaw (CVE-2026-118383) Can Crash Lagging Servers on Failover
articles.summary:
A critical flaw in MongoDB Server allows an unauthenticated attacker to send two requests that trigger a crash on the database server. The crash occurs only if that server is later chosen to take over as the main server while it still lacks some recent changes.
MongoDB, the company that makes the database, released fixed versions earlier this week.
The affected servers are members of a replica set, a group of MongoDB servers that keep copies of the same data. One member, the primary, serves as the main server and handles all new writes, while the others replicate them. If the primary becomes unavailable, the other members hold an election to pick a new primary.
Researchers at Datadog Security Labs reproduced the crash in a lab and published their findings yesterday. On vulnerable versions, turning on authentication does not stop the two requests. An attacker cannot make the targeted member fall behind or win an election, or see when either happens, the researchers said.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-118383, is a use-after-free: the server ends up using memory it has already freed. MongoDB rated it 9.5 out of 10 on the CVSS 4.0 severity scale. The company said it found the flaw itself and was "not aware of any attempts to take advantage of this vulnerability."
Affected members include the shard and config server members of sharded clusters. A standalone mongod, a single server outside any replica set, is not affected.

articles.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
articles.summary:
Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation has been stealing live Google sessions from corporate users. Every check defenders normally lean on to judge a link came back clean, and the operator designed it that way on purpose.
The Threat Research team at Material Security spotted the campaign and has since taken down hundreds of attacker domains in an effort the team calls Operation CloudFire. Here’s what the researchers found.
The lure: Google Calendar invites
The messages show up as Google Calendar invites. Some arrive by BCC, and many come from an organization the recipient has already traded email with. The pretexts are deliberately boring: voicemail notifications, RFP and RFI requests, court summonses, and missed payment notices. Nothing about them stands out in a busy inbox.
Most of the links point to Google itself. The usual pattern runs through Google’s own /url redirector, with the real destination tucked into a query parameter. Other waves used share.google and Drive file links the same way, and one variant leaned on Intuit transaction notification links. Whenever a message gets scored, the domain, certificate, and reputation on display are all legitimate.
The capture: a reverse proxy in front of Google sign-in
Once a victim clicks through, the attacker runs a live reverse proxy in front of the real Google sign-in page. The victim types a password, gets a genuine prompt, and approves it while the operator watches in real time. The server passes each second factor al…

articles.summary:
Google Cloud VMs on AMD Turin chips need a guest OS patch and a stop-and-start to protect against three CPU side-channel flaws, Google said this week.
The company has already applied mitigations against attacks between VMs, and between VMs and the host. Inside a VM, the flaws may let an attacker with code on the same processor core infer data from other processes or the kernel.
The affected machine series are C4D, N4D, H4D, Z4D,, and G4, including bare-metal instances of C4D and Z4D. Turin is the code name for fifth-generation AMD EPYC processors.
All three flaws are Transient Scheduler Attacks (TSA). Two of them, TSA-SQ (CVE-2024-36350) and TSA-L1 (CVE-2024-36357), were first disclosed on July 8, 2025, for earlier EPYC processors.
AMD now says its Zen 5 processors, which include Turin, are "impacted differently from previously characterized AMD processors." The third flaw, CVE-2026-0004, is new. It may let an attacker who can run code on a system infer data in the processor's L1 data cache.
The Xen Project, which maintains the Xen hypervisor, calls the new flaw TSA-Fill. It also says an earlier statement has been corrected: "AMD had previously said that Zen5 CPUs were not vulnerable to TSA-SQ and TSA-L1."
Google rates the issue Medium. AMD classifies all three as local attacks with high attack complexity that require only low privileges, according to its Zen 5 bulletin and CVE-2026-0004 advisory.

articles.summary:
Thursday, November 12th 2026
AMD "Siren Halo" APU Rumored to Pair Dedicated GDDR7 With LPDDR Memory
AMD's next big Halo APU might ship with two separate memory pools, if a new leak from Gotou_3rd on X is accurate. In a short post on November 12, the leaker wrote that "Siren Halo has dedicated GD7 VRAM." When asked whether that meant unified GDDR memory, like on consoles, or separate pools, Gotou clarified that LPDDR system memory would still be there. He also claimed that Siren Halo follows Medusa Halo, that Siren Point is basically a Medusa refresh, and that the new name exists because AMD won't have a fully new Halo design in 2027. There's no word on capacities, bus widths, or launch timing. AMD already added GDDR7 support to its Linux driver in September, a change widely tied to RDNA 5.
This would be quite a change for the lineup. Strix Halo and its Gorgon Halo refresh use a single LPDDR5X pool shared by the CPU and GPU, with the Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 supporting up to 192 GB, of which up to 160 GB can go to graphics. That shared pool is a big reason these chips are popular for running LLMs locally. Dedicated GDDR7 should give the iGPU far more bandwidth for gaming, though it's unclear how much memory AI workloads would get. The leaker also suggested Siren Halo could be related to Magnus, the AMD chip linked to Microsoft's Project Helix, though that is speculation at this point. AMD hasn't confirmed Siren Halo at all, so it's best treated as a rumor for now.

articles.title: 186 Fake AI Domains Redirect Users to ClickFix Lures, Browser Malware, and Search Hijackers
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers have found that lookalike domains masquerading as artificial intelligence (AI) tools are being used to serve ClickFix-style lures, browser-hijacking malware, and a set of extensions that hijack user searches.
This delivery pattern has been codenamed TypoPrompting by Island.
"AI-app lookalikes that turn an attempt to reach a familiar tool into a prompt to verify, install or run something else," the cybersecurity company said in a report shared with The Hacker News.
In all, the campaign spans 186 bogus domains spanning 27 AI brands, including Anthropic Claude, OpenAI ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM), Microsoft Copilot, SpaceXAI Grok, DeepSeek, Mistral, Perplexity, Midjourney, ElevenLabs, Lovable, and Cursor.
While one category leads to a ClickFix lure that serves a PowerShell command via a fake Cloudflare verification page, the second route takes unsuspecting users to "Security Check" pages that deliver a browser-hijacking malware called Net Guard. The third pathway sends users to a search-hijack extension family with 16 live Chrome Web Store listings and 972,000 declared users.

El FBI informó que hackers del Gobierno de Corea del Norte robaron más de USD 400 millones en criptomonedas en los últimos 18 meses con falsas videollamadas de Zoom, Microsoft Teams y Google Meet, en las que reproducen videos grabados en secreto de conocidos de la víctima.
La oficina federal llama a la maniobra “FaceStealer” (ladrón de rostros). El Departamento de Justicia anunció el mismo día la incautación de la infraestructura en la nube que usaban los atacantes, y el FBI publicó una alerta técnica con el detalle del método. La oficina ya identificó y retuvo más de 900 videos de webcam de víctimas que los hackers habían grabado para usarlos contra otras personas.
Cómo funciona la trampa
Todo empieza con una víctima previa. Los hackers toman su cuenta de Telegram u otra app de mensajes cifrados, leen sus chats y su lista de contactos, y graban su imagen mientras espera que empiece una videollamada. Después escriben a sus contactos, con su nombre, para proponer una reunión.
Los pretextos habituales son “ponerse al día”, “hablar de una colaboración” o “conversar sobre oportunidades de inversión”. Como leen el historial de mensajes, adaptan el texto a las conversaciones anteriores de cada persona, según el FBI.

articles.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Flaw Lets Attackers Read and Overwrite All Private Container Images in a Registry
articles.summary:
A critical flaw in Red Hat Quay allows an attacker who can access a Quay registry to read and overwrite private container images in every repository.
Quay enables anonymous access by default, and while it is enabled, the attacker needs no account. When it is off, anyone with a valid account can still exploit the flaw, Red Hat said yesterday. The company has released fixed builds for eight Quay 3 branches.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-123710 (CVSS score: 9.8).
Quay uses keys it trusts to sign the access tokens that allow image pushes and pulls. The flaw lets an attacker add their own key to the keys Quay trusts, with no expiry date. Quay then accepts tokens signed with that key for any repository.
With those tokens, an attacker can retrieve private images and any secrets or credentials stored within them. The attacker can also push or overwrite images, and the change propagates to every system that later pulls those images.
The planted key survives restarts until someone removes it. It can also be used to delete the keys that running Quay instances use, so normal pushes and pulls start failing with authentication errors.
Quay's key server checks that a request to replace a key carries a token signed by a trusted key, with the expected audience and issuer. It does not check whether the token was issued for key rotation. An anonymous token from Quay's /v2/auth endpoint passes: Quay signs it with a trusted key, and the caller chooses its audience.

articles.title: New SignDrop Zero-Day Exploit Turns Windows CLFS Security Feature Into SYSTEM Access
articles.summary:
Public exploit code released earlier this week claims that a local Windows user can gain SYSTEM privileges through the Common Log File System driver.
The proof of concept, called SignDrop, targets a log-authentication feature added to the driver last year. It abuses how clfs.sys creates companion files when a privileged process opens a prepared log, using path redirection to take control of the operation. Microsoft has not confirmed the claimed flaw, assigned a CVE, or released a fix.
The researcher behind the exploit, who publishes under the name MSNightmare, released the code and a detailed writeup on GitHub on Tuesday, the same day the company published its November security updates.
CLFS is a logging subsystem built into Windows. Its driver has been a frequent target for privilege escalation: 10 CLFS flaws appear in CISA's catalog of vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in attacks, including one used in ransomware campaigns in April 2025.
To reduce that exposure, Microsoft added an authentication check to CLFS log files in updates for Windows 11 25H2, 26H1, and Windows Server 2025 shipped in October 2025. The check attaches a hash-based message authentication code, built from log data and a key unique to each machine.
The driver then parses only log files it wrote. A companion .cnpf file stores recovery data beside each log and is created with the same security attributes as the original, according to the company's logfile authentication page.

articles.title: Le projet Stela pourrait faire revivre les Hackintosh
articles.summary:
Un nouveau projet open source baptisé Stela vise à pouvoir lancer macOS 27 sur des PC à processeur Intel ou AMD et carte NVIDIA. Pour l'heure, il reste toutefois au stade expérimental.
Les Hackintosh, ces PC détournés pour faire tourner macOS, semblaient condamnés depuis l’arrivée des puces ARM dans les Mac. Le projet Stela, développé par Tyler Smith et publié sur GitHub, change d’approche et fait croire à macOS qu’il tourne sur un Mac.
Un traducteur d’instructions et un pilote NVIDIA pour tromper macOS
En mars 2024, nous rapportions que les Hackintosh touchaient à leur fin. Avec macOS 14 Sonoma, Apple avait retiré les pilotes de nombreuses cartes Wi-Fi et Bluetooth. Depuis, le problème a changé de nature. MacOS 27 a abandonné les Mac Intel et reste uniquement compatible avec les puces Apple Silicon de la famille M.
Stela est un programme de démarrage UEFI, le micrologiciel qui lance un PC avant son système. Il simule du matériel Apple silicon, que macOS identifie comme un Mac mini M2. Reste que les puces Apple exécutent du code arm64e, que les processeurs Intel et AMD ne comprennent pas, puisqu’ils parlent x86-64. Un traducteur convertit donc les instructions. Il le fait à l’avance (AOT) ou à la volée (JIT). Il sait gérer plus de 3 000 formes d’instructions AArch64, le nom technique de l’arm64.
